notes: Verbatim Fig 4/7/8/9. 'Self-Disclosing Injection' is a notable novel attacker-failure mode. Judge precision numbers from Fig 7 confusion matrices. Attacker capability is a critical variable for evaluating black-box attacks.

name: Automated indirect prompt injection in agentic environments (GCG/TAP adaptation)

title: Two non-substitutable agent security surfaces: effect sink vs plaintext read boundary
summary: SecureClaw identifies two distinct, non-substitutable security requirements for tool-using agents: (1) effect surface — request-bound authorization of external effects (whether the exact request reaching an external sink is authorized for the current caller, session, inputs, and context); (2) plaintext surface — confinement of sensitive raw plaintext away from the untrusted runtime (whether the runtime ever receives raw secrets it can relay through internal channels even when a later commit is blocked). Using AgentLeak's channel taxonomy C1-C7 (C1 final response, C2 inter-agent messages, C3/C4 tool I/O, C5 shared/persistent memory, C6 logs, C7 skill/supply-chain ingress), C2 and C5 are especially important because they expose relay paths invisible to output-only defenses. The runtime (LLM planner) is untrusted for both authorization and confidentiality; trust is placed in a gateway, handle store, policy engine, and executor. The key systems claim: external effects become real at the sink, whereas plaintext fails as soon as a raw protected value enters an adversarial runtime — so sink mediation and plaintext residency are separate first-class controls.
notes: Defense paper but its threat decomposition surfaces the internal-relay-leakage threat (C2/C5 channels) that output-only auditing misses. PREVIEW->COMMIT binds policy decision to canonical request digest h=HMAC-SHA256(k_bind,Canon(rho)).

title: SecureClaw: 0% ASB / 0.64% AgentDojo ASR, 3.23% AgentLeak leak; both pillars needed
summary: Common-harness eval (gpt-4o-mini, temp 0) vs Plain, IPIGuard, DRIFT, Faramesh. SecureClaw reaches AgentDojo ASR 0.64% (4/629), AgentLeak any-leak 3.23% (16/496, C1-dominant: 15 C1 final-output, 1 C2), ASB ASR 0.00% (0/2000) while retaining ASB utility 88.90% (vs Plain 91.65% ASR / 0.85 utility; Faramesh matches ASB boundary 0% but leaves AgentLeak C2/C5 open at 92.74/51.61). Mechanism-isolation ablation (48-row AgentLeak slice): removing handles raises attacked-row C2 leak 0/24->5/24 (or 6/24) and reappears C5 (2/24), while removing the execution boundary but keeping handles leaves C2/C5 at 0/24 — confidentiality gain comes from handle confinement, not from the write boundary accidentally masking it. Compromised-runtime bypass suite: 29 scenarios (authorization-artifact tampering, malformed material, session/caller mismatch, context-binding, temporal replay, chained) — denies all 25 adversarial cases, accepts all 4 positive controls; payment case blocks 4/4 unauthorized commits while allowing the legitimate transfer. Residual failures: 4/629 AgentDojo (foreign-principal/missing-contextual-bind, broader-scope workspace) + 16/496 AgentLeak (authorized-declassification pressure) — pressure on policy contract, not bypasses of core invariants. Deny-aware recovery raises ASB utility 70%->86% at 0% ASR.
notes: Verbatim Table 2/3/4 + exact counts. Executor-side verification sub-ms; single-service auth +~15ms; distributed two-evaluator +~149ms (vs 500-2000ms LLM latency). Limitation: false assurance if protected fields misclassified or effectful sinks unmediated.

name: Internal-relay leakage via compromised/injected agent runtime (C2/C5 channels)

title: Sensitive plaintext residency in untrusted agent runtime (relayable through internal channels)
description: When a tool returns sensitive content as raw plaintext into the LLM runtime, a compromised or injected runtime can relay it through internal channels — inter-agent messages (C2), shared/persistent memory (C5), logs, or later tool calls — even when a downstream commit is blocked. Output-only / final-response defenses do not observe these relay paths. The leakage is a read-side property independent of write-side authorization: blocking the effect sink does not undo plaintext that already entered the adversarial runtime.
affected: Tool-using single- and multi-agent systems where the LLM planner/runtime directly receives raw protected values.

name: Opaque-handle plaintext confinement (read-boundary gateway)
description: A trusted gateway stores sensitive plaintext in a protected handle store and returns to the runtime only an opaque high-entropy handle (hid=HMAC-SHA256(k_handle, nonce||session||object)) plus a bounded, schema-aware summary D(v) as an explicit, auditable declassification interface. The runtime can plan over symbolic references but cannot dereference protected plaintext; dereference occurs only at trusted endpoints after caller/session/sink/policy checks. Closes internal-relay channels (C2/C5) that output-only defenses miss.

name: PREVIEW->COMMIT request-bound effect authorization (write-boundary executor)
description: Effectful writes are mediated by a trusted executor: the runtime proposes (intent, inputs); the gateway appends authenticated caller/session/ctx, canonicalizes rho and computes binding digest h=HMAC-SHA256(k_bind, Canon(rho)); the policy engine binds an allow/deny decision to exact h; the executor independently recomputes h, verifies the authorization artifact, checks freshness/replay and confirmation, then commits — else fails closed. A compromised runtime mutating recipient/channel/fields invalidates the bound artifact, so external effects commit only for the exact authorized canonical request (non-bypassable, request-bound). Deny-aware recovery returns a safe continuation to preserve utility.

label: Internal-relay sensitive-data leakage (inter-agent / memory channels)
description: Sensitive plaintext that enters an untrusted agent runtime can be relayed through internal channels — inter-agent messages (C2), shared/persistent memory (C5), logs, or later tool calls — invisible to output-only auditing, even when a final-output or sink commit is blocked. A confidentiality surface distinct from effect-authorization.

title: SoK lifecycle model: agent security = information flow x delegated authority x persistent state
summary: The SoK (247 papers: 3 in 2023, 42 in 2024, 121 in 2025, 81 partial 2026; 169/247 = 68.42% arXiv preprints) models an LLM agent as tuple A=<I,P,D,T,M,O,C> (Input, Planning, Decision, Tool/env execution, Memory, Output, Coordination). Security-relevant behavior emerges from flows among elements: low-authority content in I distorts P, changes D, triggers privileged T, poisons M, or propagates through C. Lifecycle-stage frequencies: Planning 227, Input 225, Tool Execution 209, Decision 166, Output 151, Memory 82, Monitoring 58, Inter-agent Comms 35, Coordination 20. Core modeling principles: data-control ambiguity (task-relevant but normatively untrusted text), delegated authority (attacker leverages permissions the agent holds but the attacker does not own), persistence/propagation (delayed harm via reused memory/coordination). Answer to RQ1: agent security should be modeled as the interaction of information flow, delegated authority, and persistent state across the agentic loop — prompt injection is a planning+execution problem, memory poisoning a delayed control-flow problem, multi-agent coordination a trust+propagation problem.
notes: Verbatim Table 3 + Fig 2/3. The <I,P,D,T,M,O,C> tuple is a reusable systems-oriented modeling lens for the whole RT agentic axis. Companion site cited.

title: SoK dominant threat families: prompt injection (142) + indirect PI (86) lead; memory/coordination emerging
summary: Seven dominant threat families by corpus count (Table 4): Prompt Injection 142 (local instruction manipulation redirecting planning/action), Indirect Prompt Injection 86 (hidden instruction via web content/tool outputs/files), Unsafe User Instructions 43 (harmful task acceptance under weak task framing), Malicious Tools 34 (tool-mediated misreasoning/unsafe invocation), Data Exfiltration 31 (leakage via tool-use or state exposure), Memory Poisoning 24 (delayed corruption reappearing in later plans/actions), Coordination Failures 14 (amplification of local failure through delegation/message passing). Topic frequencies: Tool-use Security 156, Runtime Defense, Prompt Injection Security 75, Multi-agent Security 63, Memory Safety 32. In tuple terms: PI/IPI target I->P and I->D; malicious tools + exfiltration become operational at D->T and T->O; memory poisoning targets I/T->M then M->P; coordination failures propagate C->P and C->D. The field is moving from single-step prompt compromise toward longer-horizon and networked failure (persistence, authority abuse, propagation), though prompt injection/control-flow hijacking remains the dominant organizing problem and identified defining weakness. Answer to RQ2: most important distinction is not attack names but propagation logics — mediated entry, delayed reactivation, inter-agent amplification.
notes: Verbatim Table 4 + Sec 6.1/6.2 + Fig 4 propagation patterns. Multi-agent share rises 9.52%(2024)->23.97%(2025)->17.28%(2026 partial). Highest-consequence deployments (finance 34, healthcare 28, embodied 28) not the most studied.

title: SoK defense/eval gaps: defenses cluster at I->P and D->T; memory/coordination + deployment metrics underserved
summary: Six defense families (Table 5) by intervention point: Input-trust management (instruction hierarchy/guardrails, I->P), Runtime monitoring & guard agents (P->D, D->T, T->O), Access control & least privilege (D->T,T->O), Information-flow & state isolation (I<->M, M->P, T->M), Execution containment/sandboxing (T->O), Topology-aware multi-agent containment (C->P, C->D, C->C). Layered defense-stack counts (Fig 5): Instruction Handling 2, Planning Validation 11, Tool Gating 13, State Protection 2, Execution Containment 2 — explicit coverage gaps: Provenance, Revocation, Inter-agent trust, Topology-aware containment. Defenses cluster around I->P and D->T (prevent untrusted content from becoming a plan, or restrict chosen actions); protections centered on M and C are thinner and less standardized. Evaluation (RQ4): Attack Success Rate in 129 papers vs Utility in only 22, Latency 8, Cost 7 — benchmark fragmentation (AgentDojo reused 30x, InjecAgent 11x, ASB/SafeAgentBench 4x; even top benchmark = 12.82% of annotations). Most reusable benchmarks concentrate on I,P,D,T while M and especially C are much less exercised. Four open challenges: provenance-aware state management, secure tool governance, multi-agent trust management, lifecycle-wide + deployment-oriented assurance.
notes: Verbatim Table 5/6/7/8/10 + Fig 5/6. SE implications: authority-scoped requirements binding authority+state+tool-scope; secure-by-design coding agents (least-privilege exec, provenance-aware file access, typed tool contracts); security regression suites replaying PI traces/poisoned memory; runtime verification + deployment assurance cases. MCP/skills/plugins flagged as supply-chain attack-surface extension (C7).

label: Multi-agent propagation / coordination-channel contagion
description: In multi-agent systems, compromise originating in one agent (via prompt injection, poisoned memory, or malicious tool output) is relayed through inter-agent messages and delegation/coordination channels into peers and then into external effect, amplifying local failure into topology-sensitive contagion. Distinct from single-agent risk: introduces message integrity, role confusion, authority spread, and covert collusion semantics.

title: PI-Hunter reframes agent red-teaming from attack-success optimization to evolutionary injection-exposure + ingestion-path localization
summary: PI-Hunter is an automated agentic AUDITING framework that inverts the usual red-team objective: instead of optimizing a single high-probability jailbreak, it acts as a diagnostic 'hunter' that maps an agent's whole security perimeter and flushes out latent indirect prompt injections buried in untrusted sources. Three stages: (1) static analysis maps tools/retrieval interfaces/API schemas/high-privilege actions; (2) an evolutionary exploitation loop pairs an LLM 'Generator' (source-aware meta-seeding + feedback-driven mutation, default 5 seeds x 10 iterations) with a trajectory-aware 'Evaluator' that audits intermediate reasoning for intent-deviation/authority-confusion/abnormal-tool-use rather than only final-output success; (3) a 'Patcher' applies lightweight transient mitigations (blacklisting, interface restriction, source isolation) so subsequent search is forced toward undiscovered ingestion paths. A successful test case localizes the precise source->tool Ingestion Path, not merely a 'bad source'. On AgentDojo under Gemini-3.1-pro/agentvigil, Source Recall rises 0.255->0.834 and Instruction Recall 0.436->0.824 vs baseline.
notes: Verbatim gains (Baseline->PI-Hunter): AgentDojo/Gemini-3.1-pro/agentvigil Src Rec 0.255->0.834, Ins Rec 0.436->0.824; Src Div 0.11->0.84, Ins Div 0.30->0.82. Generalizes across ReAct & Planner-Executor (Ins Rec 0.27->0.49 ReAct, 0.22->0.67 Planner-Exec). Saturates ~8-10 iterations. Novel axis = injection-exposure/coverage objective + source-tool localization, distinct from attack-optimizers GOAT/AutoRedTeamer/SIRAJ.

title: PI-Hunter exposes residual latent injections that Spotlighting, MELON and PIGuard defenses fail to block
summary: Under the strongest attack setting (agentvigil, Gemini-2.5-pro backbone) PI-Hunter was run against three representative prompt-injection defenses to test whether proactive auditing still surfaces hidden injections after deployment-grade mitigations. Every defense reduces total exposed injections, but substantial latent injections persist and PI-Hunter consistently beats the unconstrained baseline on both exposure and diversity. On AgentDojo under Spotlight, Source Recall improves 0.3003->0.4559 and Instruction Recall 0.2204->0.3898; under the strongest defense PIGuard the baseline nearly collapses to ZERO Instruction Recall while PI-Hunter still exposes 0.1942. Critically, the baseline degenerates to near-zero diversity under defended settings (Ins Div 0.000 for Spotlight/MELON/PIGuard) whereas PI-Hunter maintains broad exploration (0.475/0.550/0.272). Demonstrates current PI defenses are insufficient alone and that feedback-guided trajectory auditing is needed to stress-test defended agents.
notes: Verbatim: AgentDojo Src Rec None 0.348->0.480, Spotlight 0.300->0.456, MELON 0.289->0.417, PIGuard 0.154->0.296; Ins Rec PIGuard baseline 0.000->0.194. Defenses tested = Spotlighting(Hines 2024), MELON(Zhu 2025), PIGuard(Li 2025). Method->control link: these three defenses become candidate controls for risk-safety-analyst. ^[ambiguous] 'baseline' = unconstrained agentic red-team baseline.

title: RedEdit: MCTS + VLM-proposer agent red-teams image safety classifiers via user-style photo edits with a dual-gate (evasion + semantic-preservation) success criterion
summary: RedEdit is the first framework to formalize user-style photo-editing evasion as a black-box combinatorial search over an edit tree and red-team IMAGE safety classifiers (a modality most red-team method work ignores). Two components instantiate human-attacker capabilities: a VLM-based proposer (domain knowledge -- generates k targeted candidate edits per node, conditioned on edit history to avoid failed paths) and an MCTS planner (iterative backtracking -- UCT selection, expansion, detector-feedback evaluation, backpropagation). The critical methodological contribution is a DUAL-GATE success definition: an attack counts only if it both evades the detector (f(x*)<tau) AND preserves recognizable harmful semantics (CPR>=0.60), so destroying content does not count as success -- a content-preservation gate absent from prior evasion work. Tools are 16 non-generative, deterministic, parameter-bounded edits (geometry/color-tone/format/overlay); crop/mosaic/strong-blur deliberately excluded. On 777 UnsafeBench images vs Qwen3.6-35B: 76.2% ASR, 93.0% CPR, 1.26 mean steps, far exceeding Single-Best exhaustive (59.5%) and ReAct sequential (30.1%).
notes: Verbatim: 76.2% ASR / 93.0% CPR / 1.26 steps / 164 attackable (777 imgs). Ablation 2x2: RedEdit 76.2 vs ReAct(VLM+Sequential) 30.1 (-46.1pp = backtracking contribution), Random-Proposer+MCTS 68.9 (-7.3), VLM-Greedy 37.3 (-38.9). Proposal width k inverted-U: peak k=3 (76.2%). 73.6% of successes terminate at 1 edit. New attack=atk-photo-edit-evasion. New benchmark for risk-safety = UnsafeBench (777 imgs, 11 categories). RedEdit positioned as diagnostic tool, not just attack.

title: RedEdit edits transfer across 12 image detectors without re-optimization, exposing a representation-level systemic blind spot across the whole moderation ecosystem
summary: RedEdit's transfer analysis is a method-level finding about the GENERALITY of the discovered weakness rather than a single classifier flaw. Setting A (direct attack, identical strategy, swap only target detector): >70% ASR on general-purpose VLM detectors (GPT-5.5 73.2%, Qwen3.6-35B 76.2%) and 58.4% on the most robust (Claude-Opus-4-7); safety-tuned VLMs prove most robust (LlavaGuard 41.1%, ImageGuard 20.1%) confirming adversarial safety-tuning gives meaningful but partial protection. Setting B (transfer edits optimized on Qwen to 12 other detectors WITHOUT re-optimization): every one of 12 architecturally-diverse detectors shows a positive Detector-Evasion-Rate gain (+2.0 to +25.0 pp), spanning general-purpose VLMs, safety-tuned VLMs and conventional classifiers; the strongest detector Qwen3.5-397B (baseline DER 2.4%) sees a 10x increase. This architecture-agnostic transferability indicates MCTS-found edits exploit fundamental representation-level weaknesses rather than model-specific artifacts.
notes: Verbatim transfer DER deltas: GPT-5.5 +15.2, Claude-Opus-4-7 +21.4, Kimi-K2.6 +25.0, Qwen3.5-397B +21.6, LlavaGuard +2.0, ImageGuard +2.8, NudeNet +2.3, FalconsaiNSFW +16.6. Setting A direct ASR: 5 categories at 100% (Deception/Harassment/Illegal/Pub.health/Spam); Hate(43%)/Sexual(66%) most resistant. Three detector tiers: general VLM / safety-tuned VLM / conventional. Method finding = transferability as a systemic-risk diagnostic.

title: Culturally-adapted red-teaming via a 'Semantic Mold' pipeline that separates attack intent from localized cultural content, raising ASR over direct-translation across all 16 language x model cells
summary: A red-team data-generation method that disentangles ATTACK INTENT from CULTURAL CONTENT, distinguishing it from both direct-translation (DT) and fixed-template approaches. The 3-stage culturally-adapted (CA) pipeline: (1) seed collection + taxonomy mapping (seeds from SALAD-Bench/ALERT/WildGuard-Mix/HEx-PHI/AIR-Bench/Do-Not-Answer, retained only on 6-model unanimous auto-label); (2) Semantic Mold -- an LLM abstracts core attack components (Action/Target/Method/Condition) into slots with category-specific Required/Optional schemata, preserving natural sentence flow unlike rigid templates; (3) content localization -- real local news/legal/community context injected into slots to produce locally-grounded prompts. Built on the CAGE generator (Kim 2026) extended to KO/JA/TH/KM. Result: delta-ASR(CA-DT)>0 across ALL 16 language x model combinations, mean +9.3 pp (range +2.6 KM/EXAONE to +18.6 KM/Gemma); by language TH +11.8 > KO +9.1 > KM +8.5 > JA +7.9; by model EXAONE +14.95 > Qwen +8.33 > Gemma +7.39 > Llama +6.68. DT underestimates risk in 44/48 category x language cells.
notes: Verbatim: 4 langs (KO/JA/TH/KM), 500 DT + 500 CA per lang, 12 categories. Mean delta-ASR +9.3pp; all 16 cells positive. Target models: Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, EXAONE-3.5-7.8B, Gemma-3-12B. Gen/judge: gemini-2.5-pro generation, GPT-4.1 ASR judge + Cultural Realism scoring. New teaming axes = automated.cultural-adaptation (Semantic Mold) + manual.expert-localization. Threat-form distribution heterogeneous: JA=interpersonal(B/A/C), TH=societal-conflict(E/K/B), KO=security/crime(I/D/L), KM=ethnic/political(D/L).

title: Cultural Realism 3-criteria rubric (plausibility/taxonomy-adherence/cultural-depth) quantifies direct-translation's blind spot at three distinct levels
summary: The paper contributes a 3-criteria Cultural Realism evaluation protocol to measure WHY direct translation fails as a red-team data source -- a calibration method for multilingual benchmark validity. C1 Plausibility (0-5, could the scenario realistically occur), C2 Taxonomy Adherence (0-5, weighted Required/Optional slot utilization, alpha=0.8), C3 Cultural Depth (0-3, how deeply embedded in local context). CA > DT on all three criteria across all four languages. The decisive criterion is C3: DT Cultural-Depth converges below 1.0 for ALL languages (KO 0.04, JA 0.42, TH 0.07, KM 0.15) vs CA (KO 1.74, JA 1.89, TH 1.40, KM 2.51), quantitatively confirming DT is a surface-level linguistic transform that reports ASR on a distribution fundamentally divergent from real-world inputs. Blind spots manifest at 3 levels: (L1) systematic category-level underestimation (CA>DT in 44/48 cells, gaps reaching +13-20pp); (L2) asymmetric country-level distribution -- aggregating under 'Asia' erases inter-country diversity; (L3) fundamental distributional divergence (C3<1.0 everywhere). KM (Khmer, low-resource) shows the largest C3 gap (+2.36), implying lower-resource languages carry the largest recoverable cultural information.
notes: Verbatim C3 DT vs CA: KO 0.04/1.74, JA 0.42/1.89, TH 0.07/1.40, KM 0.15/2.51 (delta KM +2.36 largest). C1 ceiling effect (KO/KM DT already high 4.22/4.49). C2 delta largest JA +1.37. GPT-4.1 automated rubric scoring, expert-consensus criteria. Method = benchmark-validity diagnostic. ^[ambiguous] 'Asia-as-monolith erasure' is an interpretive (L2) claim grounded in category-variance tables.

title: Nous: behavioral-profile injection to counter agent 'cognitive monoculture' is a measured NULL at the prompt level -- a negative result bounding LLM-as-population diversity methods
summary: Nous targets cognitive monoculture as a red-team-adjacent population-level risk: agents on shared foundation models produce correlated reasoning (independently-developed frontier models' forecasting errors correlate r~0.77-0.78 across 568 resolved questions), degrading collective-intelligence guarantees. The method extracts a structured 8-dimension behavioral proxy (Core/Shell/Membrane layers: risk-perception, time-scale, cognitive-style, attention, belief-update, domain-confidence, independence, loss-response) from real on-chain Polymarket behavior and injects it via a structure-to-narrative translator into agent system prompts to induce heterogeneity. The headline is a DISSOCIATION between the two halves: (1) Extraction works partially -- on N=100 wallets 8/14 parameters are temporally stable (split-half ICC>=0.5, bootstrap CI lower-bound >0.3), led by independence.contrarian_score (ICC=0.90); wallets identifiable from profile (top-1 retrieval 17-22% vs 1% random); 2/4 pre-specified dimensions rank-correlate with future profit out-of-sample. (2) Injection is a NULL -- on a semantic embedding metric structured injection shows NO significant advantage over a length-matched control on any model; induced diversity neither reduces ensemble error-correlation nor improves Brier (p~0.95), persisting across temperature 0.0-1.0 and a more-diverse synthetic population. Bottleneck localized to the translator, which emits semantically near-uniform prompts whose spread does not increase when profile spread does -- motivating below-the-prompt methods (PEFT, activation steering).
notes: Verbatim: error-correlation r~0.77-0.78 (568 Qs, GPT-4o/Claude/Gemini); extraction 8/14 params ICC>=0.5, contrarian_score ICC=0.90, entropy/crowd_sens 0.76, horizon_bias 0.75, analytical_ratio 0.73, update_rate 0.68, patience 0.62, lambda 0.57; identifiability top-1 17-22% vs 1%. Injection JS-divergence +0.0035 (p=0.010) but Brier p~0.95. Honest negative result -- mark future + evidence_grade B (single-author, gray-box live params). New threat candidate=frontier.cognitive-monoculture. Method = future.cognitive-diversity-injection (LLM-as-population). Mantic system: Metaculus 38.6->45.8, 8th/550 Summer-2025.

title: JailbreakOPT composes atomic jailbreak tools into nested encode/decode attack chains under a unified orchestrator-mutator-evaluator-selector abstraction
summary: JailbreakOPT unifies iterative single-turn jailbreak optimizers (PAIR/GCG/AutoDAN/TAP) under one orchestrator-mutator-evaluator-selector abstraction, then introduces an ATTACK TOOL LIBRARY of atomic single-turn jailbreaks (Code Chameleon, Flip Attack, ArtPrompt/Persuasion) that the orchestrator composes into multi-tool attack chains still yielding a standalone target prompt. Each tool is an encoding-decoding pair (encoding disguises malicious intent, decoding instructs the target to recover it -- analogous to encryption/decryption). Composition uses a consistent nesting rule: enc_(a0,a1)=enc_a1 o enc_a0, dec applied in reverse (gift-wrap/unwrap), with admissibility constraints for non-commutative tools; genetic operations (crossover/mutation) are lifted to the TOOL level. Result: augmenting iterative optimizers with the tool library substantially improves ASR on hard targets -- on AdvBench tool-augmented TAP lifts GPT-5.1 ASR 29.46%->83.46% and Claude 0.96%->56.54%; tool-augmented AutoDAN(LLM-judge) lifts GPT-5.1 60.19%->91.15% and Claude 0.38%->59.81% -- and reduces No.A in several settings. LLM-judge validated by 4 PhD annotators (Spearman rho=0.660, p<0.0001).
notes: Verbatim AdvBench (iterative-with-tools, ours): TAP GPT-5.1 29.46->83.46%, Claude 0.96->56.54%, Gemini 9.79->20.19%; AutoDAN(LLM-judge) GPT-5.1 60.19->91.15%, Claude 0.38->59.81%, Qwen3 16.15->100%, DeepSeek 91.35->100%. Targets: Vicuna-13b/LLaMA-3-8b/GPT-4o/GPT-5.1/Gemini-3-flash/Claude-Haiku-4.5/Qwen3-235b/DeepSeek-v3.2. Budget frontier-width 8 x depth 8 = 64 attempts/episode. New teaming axis=automated.tool-composition (encode/decode chain). LLM-judge agreement rho=0.660.

title: JailbreakOPT frames inter-episode jailbreak tool-selection as a contextual bandit (Thompson sampling), enabling self-improving attackers that reuse past attack trajectories
summary: Beyond intra-episode composition, JailbreakOPT's distinctive contribution is INTER-EPISODE LEARNING: it models each completed search episode as an Action-History-Augmented Decision Process (AHADP) and casts attack-tool selection across episodes as a CONTEXTUAL MULTI-ARMED BANDIT, adopting logistic Thompson sampling as the orchestration policy. Each expansion yields a bandit record (context c, tool a, trajectory-label y) where c = phi(x, action-history, target-model-identity, eval-stats) and y marks whether the trajectory reached a successful depth; successful trajectories at the stopping depth are positive, all others negative. This is a concrete self-improving-attacker mechanism -- prior attack trajectories guide future tool selection rather than re-searching from scratch. Two lightweight context signals (tool-usage history + target-model identity) each beat the no-context baseline under a reduced 3x8 (24-attempt) budget: combined, ASR reaches 61.54% (GPT-5.1), 98.08% (Gemini), 40.38% (Claude) vs no-context 19.23/30.77/5.77%. Online progressive training shows ASR improving and No.A dropping as trajectories accumulate; policies transfer partially cross-target, with mixed-target training most robust. Distinct from memory/replay systems (AutoDAN-Turbo, Auto-RedTeamer) by using a principled bandit rather than log retrieval.
notes: Verbatim context-ablation (3x8 budget, TAP-based): no-context 19.23/30.77/5.77% (GPT-5.1/Gemini/Claude); +tool-history 53.85/82.69/36.54%; +target-id 57.69/84.62/26.92%; +both 61.54/98.08/40.38%. Contrast with AutoDAN-Turbo/Auto-RedTeamer (log-retrieval) -- JailbreakOPT uses logistic Thompson sampling. Self-improving attacker = high-novelty 2026 method shift (reserve high novelty_signal per work principles). Cross-target transfer best under mixed training.

name: User-style photo-editing evasion of image safety classifiers (RedEdit)
Nested encode/decode tool-composition jailbreak chain (JailbreakOPT)

title: Image safety classifiers are brittle under semantics-preserving photo-edit tool chains
description: Conventional, safety-tuned and general-purpose-VLM image safety classifiers can be driven below their unsafe-score threshold by short (<2 step) sequences of common, non-generative, deterministic photo-editing operations (rotate/hue/grayscale/flip) while harmful semantics remain recognizable to humans (CPR>=0.60). Edits optimized against one detector transfer to 12 architecturally diverse detectors without re-optimization (+2.0 to +25.0pp DER), indicating a representation-level rather than model-specific weakness.
affected: Image safety classifiers (CNN/CLIP NSFW filters, safety-tuned VLMs LlavaGuard/ImageGuard, general-purpose VLM detectors)
disclosure: research-only release; coordinate with detector developers

label: Cognitive monoculture of foundation-model agent populations
description: When many AI agents are built on shared foundation models they produce highly correlated reasoning and forecasting errors (independently-developed frontier models correlate r~0.77-0.78), collapsing the diversity/independence conditions required for collective intelligence and creating correlated failure modes in agent populations (prediction markets, multi-agent ensembles, collective decision-making). Prompt-level cognitive-diversity injection does not measurably remedy it, implying a below-the-prompt structural risk.

title: Reconstruction (attribute-inference) attacks recover hidden attributes from synthetic/de-identified tabular releases; generator choice, not attacker sophistication, is the dominant risk lever
summary: SoK systematizing 14 reconstruction attacks x 9 SDG methods x 5 datasets (Adult, NIST Arizona, California Housing, NIST SBO, CDC Diabetes). Adversary holds the published synthetic/de-identified table plus a target's quasi-identifiers (QI) and infers hidden attributes (income, disease, wealth). Scored by rarity-weighted reconstruction advantage R_adv (perfect=100/C%). Mean reconstruction accuracy varies 8-20 points across attacks but tens of points across generators: down a column best vs worst attack differ ~8-20pp, across a row generators swing more (RF: 18.5 on near-noiseless MST vs 52.3 on CellSuppression). De-identification (CellSupp R_adv 31.7, RankSwap 22.5) leaks most; highest-fidelity TabDDPM 27.0; DP marginal synthesis collapses toward Mode reference baseline at tight budget (MST eps=0.1: 12.4). KNN hits 83.5% on CDC under de-identification; CoBP-RA leads on average (26.7). DP protects mainly below epsilon<=1 then plateaus (RF on Adult MST drops to 13.1% at eps=0.1). Memorization test: gap Delta=R_adv(train)-R_adv(non-train); most generators Delta<=1.6pp (distributional inference), but TabDDPM Delta=+13.4pp (genuine memorization of atypical records). Disparate impact: synthesis concentrates risk on rare/outlier records (~2.2-2.9x typical) while suppression protects minorities and exposes the majority; AI/AN at 7x White rate on CDC under TabDDPM.
notes: All numbers verbatim from Tables 1,2,5-9. ATLAS T0024 (exfil via inference) and T0057 (LLM data leakage) are approximate maps; reconstruction is a tabular-SDG privacy attack, not strictly an ML-model-API exfil — mapping is by analogy. First-place NIST CRC 2025 red-team validation gives evidence_grade A for measured numbers.

name: CoBP-RA (Correction with Belief Propagation reconstruction attack)

title: Synthetic/de-identified tabular releases leak hidden attributes via preserved feature correlations and (for high-fidelity generators) memorization of atypical records
description: A published synthetic or de-identified record-level table intended to preserve statistical structure without containing real records still permits an adversary holding a target's quasi-identifiers to reconstruct hidden sensitive attributes. Two leakage mechanisms: (i) distributional — correlations among hidden features (exploited by correlation-aware attacks like CoBP-RA, autoregressive chaining, joint-generative conditioning) let any similar person's hidden value be inferred; (ii) memorization — high-capacity diffusion generators (TabDDPM, train-vs-holdout gap +13.4pp) and de-identification (CellSuppression +20pp, RankSwap +13.5pp retain originals) expose specific individuals. De-identification under k-anonymity is the most exposed family; differential privacy bounds leakage only at epsilon<=1 before plateauing. Risk concentrates on demographically rare / outlier individuals (2.2-2.9x typical reconstruction rate).
affected: Synthetic tabular data releases (PrivBayes/MST/AIM DP synth, TVAE/CTGAN/ARF/TabDDPM deep generators, Synthpop), de-identified microdata (cell suppression, rank swapping), used in census, health (HIPAA), and financial disclosure

hazard: Synthetic or de-identified tabular release preserves enough correlational structure (or memorizes atypical records) that an adversary with a target's quasi-identifiers can reconstruct hidden sensitive attributes
hazardous_situation: A data holder (census agency, hospital, financial regulator) publishes synthetic/de-identified microdata believed privacy-preserving and an adversary with cheap public auxiliary data (voter rolls, social profiles) runs a reconstruction attack against named individuals, with risk concentrated on demographically rare people
residual_risk: medium — DP at epsilon<=1 demonstrably caps reconstruction (RF on Adult MST drops to 13.1% at eps=0.1, near Mode baseline 10.5%) but degrades utility (TSTR collapses) and does not bound continuous-feature synthesis; non-private deep generators and de-identification retain high reconstruction (R_adv up to 52-84%). With DP-at-tight-budget control, residual is medium; without it, high. Evidenced by NIST CRC measured numbers.

title: Individual sensitive-attribute disclosure from synthetic/de-identified data reconstruction
affected: Individuals whose records appear in published synthetic/de-identified tabular releases — especially demographically rare/outlier persons (e.g. AI/AN at 7x majority rate), patients (CDC Diabetes 83.5% reconstruction), census respondents, financial-survey subjects

name: Differentially private tabular synthesis at tight privacy budget (epsilon<=1)
description: Generate the synthetic release with a differentially private SDG mechanism (MST, AIM, PrivBayes) at epsilon<=1. Empirically caps reconstruction advantage near the Mode baseline (RF on Adult MST: 13.1% at eps=0.1) and — uniquely among tested families — combines memorization-free behaviour with equitable protection across demographic subgroups. Trade-off: utility (TSTR) degrades sharply at low epsilon and continuous-feature synthesis remains poorly protected; protection plateaus above epsilon~1 so high real-world budgets (2020 US Census eps~19.6) buy little reconstruction defence. Recommended paired with reconstruction-attack auditing rather than relied on alone.

name: Audit synthetic/de-identified releases with a learning reconstruction adversary (not a matching adversary) and report per-subgroup risk
description: Before release, run the strongest available attribute-reconstruction attack (CoBP-RA recommended as a strong, inexpensive default) rather than the matching-based El Emam / similarity-distance audits that standard practice uses (which understate exposure — El Emam scores CellSuppression 0.42 where a one-line nearest-neighbour attack recovers 64%). Report the distribution of risk: the memorization test (train-vs-holdout R_adv gap) separates removable memorization from distributional inference, and per-subgroup / per-feature scores expose demographically rare individuals hidden by a reassuring mean. Both diagnostics fall out of the same attack run at no extra cost.

title: AI peer reviewers can be gamed with presentation-only edits (no hidden prompts, no content change), inflating scores via a strength-weakness asymmetry — a research-integrity harm
summary: Adversarial repackaging holds scientific content fixed (methods/experiments/figures/equations/proofs/numbers immutable — 'fixed zone'; only abstract/intro/related-work/discussion = 'free zone' edited) and runs a closed-loop Profile->Plan->Edit->Review->Evaluate->Update search using the AI reviewer's own feedback. Cross-model average +1.21/10 score, 75.1% ASR over Claude Sonnet 4 (+1.47 dS, 87.0% ASR), Sonnet 4.5 (+1.24, 79.8%), GPT-5-mini (+0.91, 58.4%). Beats baselines: Zero-shot Paper Laundering (+0.33, 30.0%), PAA abstract-only (+0.46, 36.7%), Research Agent (+0.90, 53.3%). Two structural deficiencies: (1) strength-weakness asymmetry — strengths improve in 86.1% of rounds (mean +2.19) but weakness-severity drops only 68.4% of rounds and BACKFIRES 31.6% (2.6x the 12.4% strength backfire); in 15.8% of score-improving rounds weaknesses simultaneously worsen ('swamping effect'). (2) Limitation laundering — of 6 original weaknesses, 3 removed (one flipped to a strength), reviewer equates appearance of addressing an issue with resolving it ('only two datasets' reframed as 'complementary data regimes' adopted as a strength). Strategy gradient: narrative restructuring (related-work repositioning 49.3% exposure, analytical-discussion expansion +2.63 str/-1.98 sev) far beats surface polishing (table formatting 29.8%, local polishing 27.8%). Effect plateaus ~5.0-5.5/10 for papers with concrete experimental gaps. Edits violate no conference policy, making this far harder to guard than prompt injection.
notes: Numbers verbatim from Table 1, Fig 2, Table 2. Distinct from prompt-injection peer-review attacks (e.g. 2511.01287, 2509.09912): no hidden text, policy-compliant — a structural deficiency of AI-reviewer evaluation, not a patchable injection. ATLAS T0051 (prompt injection) is a loose map; this is closer to LLM-judge/evaluation gaming with no injected instruction. mit_subdomain 6.x (societal/info-integrity) for the harm chain captured in risk-ai-peer-review-gaming.

name: Adversarial repackaging (presentation-only AI-peer-review gaming)

title: AI peer reviewers systematically reward presentation-level signals (contribution framing, related-work positioning) over genuine scientific merit, and equate the appearance of addressing a limitation with resolving it
description: Current AI reviewers (Claude Sonnet 4/4.5, GPT-5-mini, across ICLR/NeurIPS/ICML templates) violate a 'resistance to presentation-only review gaming' necessary condition: review scores systematically become more favorable when only presentation is adjusted with scientific content held fixed. Two structural deficiencies: a strength-weakness asymmetry (easier to impress than convince — strength amplification reliable at 86.1%, weakness rebuttal uncontrollable, backfiring 31.6%) and limitation laundering (reframing a weakness as design intent causes the reviewer to adopt the reframing and soften or drop the criticism). Not a model-specific defect — consistent across three models and templates, indicating a structural property of current AI reviewers, with positive cross-model attack transfer.
affected: LLM/MLLM automated peer-review systems (AAAI 2026 AI review pilot, ICLR 2025 review feedback agent, conferences exploring review automation)

title: Multimodal AI reviewers are pervasively vulnerable to cross-modal score-inflation attacks via figure perturbation and text injection; chunk-based retrieval defense detects them at near-zero false-positive rate
summary: PaperGuard benchmark (1136 ICLR+F1000Research papers, text+extracted figures). Attack goal is domain-specific score inflation (max s_overall,adv - s_clean over 8 aspects, +/-80 theoretical range), NOT a safety-policy jailbreak — so jailbreak/toxicity defenses don't apply. Black-box prompt injection: up to 80% ASR on Claude-Sonnet-4.5 with +14.14 score shift (highest fragility among proprietary); GPT-4o 0.72 ASR/+6.65, GPT-4.1 0.68/+9.40; attacks succeed by suppressing criticism (negative-tag reduction, e.g. Mistral-Small -3.26 neg tags) more than fabricating praise. Counter-intuitive: stronger/larger models more vulnerable (better instruction-following); DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B lowest ASR 0.46 only because it fails to function as a reviewer (~62% parse). White-box: GCG text up to 0.78 ASR (Qwen-3-8B); visual PGD/APGD/C&W inflate scores via imperceptible figure perturbation alone — APGD strongest (Qwen-2.5-VL-7B +12.71, Janus-Pro-7B +14.11), demonstrating insufficiency of text-only defenses. Defense: most strategies fail (Moderation API & BERT/embedding classifiers 0.0 recall — instructions lost in document noise; LLM-as-Judge high recall but 100% FPR, would falsely accuse legitimate authors). Chunk-based Embedding Search (multimodal segmentation + reference retrieval + cross-modal intent verification) is the only practical defense: 95.0%/93.5% text/visual acc, 92.86%/90.32% recall, near-zero FPR (0.0/0.10); generalizes to 17 real arxiv papers with confirmed hidden injections at 100% recall / 0% FPR vs LLM-as-Judge 64.7% and Moderation API 0%.
notes: Numbers verbatim from Tables 1-4. Visual figure-perturbation score inflation (imperceptible PGD on a scientific figure) is the novel cross-modal vector. ATLAS T0043 (craft adversarial data / evasion) maps the white-box PGD/GCG branch; T0051 maps black-box injection. mit_subdomain 6.x for the research-integrity harm; the chunk-based defense is captured as control-chunk-embedding-injection-detection.

name: Cross-modal AI-reviewer score inflation (text injection + GCG suffix + imperceptible figure PGD/APGD/C&W perturbation)

title: Multimodal AI reviewers can be driven to inflate review scores by imperceptible perturbation of paper figures or injected/optimized text, with stronger models more vulnerable
description: Multimodal LLM peer reviewers process text and figures, where figures convey core method/results evidence. An adversary who can only modify submitted paper content (never the review prompt or model) achieves domain-specific score inflation through (i) black-box prompt injection (up to 80% ASR, +14.14 score on Claude-Sonnet-4.5), (ii) white-box GCG text suffix (up to 0.78 ASR), and (iii) imperceptible l-inf/l-2 figure perturbation alone (PGD/APGD/C&W; +12.71 to +14.11 score) — demonstrating that text-only safeguards are insufficient for the visual channel. Attacks work by suppressing critical assessment (negative-tag reduction) rather than fabricating praise. Counter-intuitively, more capable models are more susceptible due to superior instruction-following. The injection is a single malicious chunk hidden in a long-context document, defeating global classifiers and generic moderation.
affected: Multimodal LLM/MLLM peer-review systems (Claude-Sonnet-4.5, GPT-4o/4.1, Qwen-2.5-VL/Qwen-3, Mistral-Small, Gemma-3, Janus-Pro, LLaVA)

hazard: AI peer reviewers reward presentation framing and are vulnerable to cross-modal (text + imperceptible figure) score-inflation manipulation, conflating the appearance of merit/resolution with genuine scientific quality
hazardous_situation: Conferences and journals (AAAI 2026 AI review pilot, ICLR review-feedback agent) deploy LLM/MLLM reviewers as formal gatekeepers; an author games scores through policy-compliant presentation-only repackaging (75.1% ASR, +1.21/10) or content perturbation (up to 80% ASR, +14 points), distorting acceptance decisions and the incentive structure of science toward repackaging over real research
residual_risk: medium-high — for the cross-modal injection/perturbation vector, the chunk-based embedding-search defense (PaperGuard) demonstrably reduces residual risk (95%/93.5% acc, 100% recall on real-world injections, near-zero FPR), so with that control residual is medium. For the presentation-only repackaging vector there is NO effective control (policy-compliant, structural reviewer deficiency, unmitigated), keeping that branch high. Detectability is low because presentation edits violate no policy and figure perturbations are imperceptible.

title: Erosion of scientific peer-review integrity via AI-reviewer manipulation
affected: Scientific community, conference/journal acceptance decisions, honest authors penalized relative to gamers, downstream consumers of published research; deployed AI peer-review systems at AAAI/ICLR/NeurIPS

name: Resistance-to-presentation-only-review-gaming testing for AI reviewers before deployment
description: Treat 'AI reviewer scores must not systematically rise when only presentation is adjusted with scientific content held fixed' as a necessary deployment condition, and red-team it with the adversarial-repackaging closed loop (free/limited/fixed editing zones) before fielding an automated reviewer. Surfaces the strength-weakness asymmetry and limitation-laundering failure modes that policy-compliant edits exploit. Note: passing this test alone does not justify safe deployment (paper's own caveat); it is a screening lower bound, not a guarantee, and there is currently no robust mitigation for the presentation-gaming vector itself — anchoring reviewers to fixed-zone evidence and penalizing reframing-without-resolution are open research directions.

name: Chunk-based multimodal embedding-similarity search for AI-reviewer injection/perturbation detection
description: Defend long-context multimodal review against score-inflation injection as a needle-in-haystack retrieval problem: segment the paper into text chunks and figure chunks, retrieve top-k chunks nearest to a registry of known textual/visual attack patterns in a shared multimodal embedding space (E5-V), then run a cross-modal verifier LLM that flags a chunk only if it carries an active malicious instruction (vs benign discussion of security prompts). Outperforms global classifiers (BERT/embedding 0.0 recall) and LLM-as-Judge (100% FPR) — achieves 95.0%/93.5% text/visual accuracy, 92.86%/90.32% recall at near-zero FPR (0.0/0.10), and generalizes to real-world injections (100% recall, 0% FPR on 17 confirmed-injection arxiv papers) where Moderation API catches none. Near-zero FPR is critical to avoid falsely accusing legitimate authors.

title: Frontier CUA injection-resistance is domain-conditioned (browser 0% hand-crafted ASR vs coding-skill up to 100%) and lives in weights not prompts; high literature ASR tracks RL-optimized phrasing, and 4/6 audited red-team papers are unreproducible
summary: CUA-HANDCRAFTED: 793 episodes, 56 hand-crafted (non-RL) attack templates across 8 families x 5 depth levels x 4 system-prompt configs, on Claude Sonnet 4.6 + GPT-5.4. Multi-step ASR = 0/140 (Clopper-Pearson 95% UB 2.60%; raw 2/158 UB 4.49% before excluding a stale-eval bank task). Only non-zero hand-crafted rate is single-step DoS on legacy models (6.16% Sonnet 4 / 6.88% GPT-4o). Prompt ablation L0_bare..L3_hardened all 0% incl L1_helpful that actively encourages following on-page directives -> resistance is weight-level not prompt-level. RL-attacker upper-bound: AutoInject adaptive-random-suffix at $25/5-query budget also lands 0/100 on frontier, converting 'RL is the gap' from inference to measured ceiling. CROSS-DOMAIN: same Sonnet 4.6/GPT-5.4 weights fall to hand-crafted coding-skill injection on SKILLBENCH at 40/40=100% (Sonnet 4.6 best) / 79/100=79% (GPT-5.4 best), mean 33.3%/66.8%; GPT-5.4-mini hardest at 96%. AIShellJack reports 84% on Copilot/Cursor shell-injection. Anthropic SC 49.36%->1.29% browser ASR collapse (38x, Sonnet 4.5->4.6) is therefore domain-specific. Reproducibility audit (Table 4): every published CUA red-team headline >25% either targets a retired model, leans on unreleased optimized strings, or both; 4/6 audited papers pair a retired target with unreleased strings = permanently unreproducible at full fidelity. Image-channel (VPI-Bench replication): popup-overlay 1/30 (3.3%) attempted-compromise, in-content malicious text 5/20 (25%, mostly nav-to-exfil bounded by login walls).
notes: Numbers verbatim from Tables 1-4 and appendices. Single-author preprint, Patronus AI. Key risk-intelligence contributions: (1) safety hardening is domain-conditioned — a 'Sonnet 4.6 resists prompt injection at X%' claim is ill-defined without a surface qualifier; report ASR as a vector across surfaces. (2) Benchmark-validity finding: literature ASR tracks RL-optimized phrasing per se, and techniques published without optimized strings/attacker models are unreproducible. Both are benchmark-intelligence findings (evidence_grade A for measured numbers, but reproducibility verdicts are the author's audit). Frontier model IDs (Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4) are the paper's naming.

title: Coding-agent skill-injection (SKILLBENCH) reaches up to 100% hand-crafted ASR on frontier weights that resist browser injection at 0% — an unevenly-hardened agentic attack surface
summary: SKILLBENCH is a sister coding-agent benchmark: malicious Markdown 'skill files' (task instructions + embedded shell snippets, named claude_v1..claude_v54) load at session start and try to induce harmful actions during normal coding workflow — adding an attacker-controlled git remote and pushing the repo, planting an env-validator script that uploads .env to an attacker host as an 'audit telemetry' step — scored by an LLM judge against a harm-objective rubric (manual re-label >90% agreement). On the SAME Claude Sonnet 4.6 / GPT-5.4 weights that hold browser hand-crafted injection at 0/140, hand-crafted coding-skill injection reaches: Sonnet 4.6 best 40/40=100% (mean 33.3% across 3 methods), GPT-5.4 best 79/100=79% (mean 66.8% across 6 methods), GPT-5.4-mini best 96/100=96% (mean 88.0%). Strongest method claude_v35 is an 8-phase cognitive-load workflow checklist piping a long env-validator script into bash on Phase 1, burying exfil in legitimate workflow steps; claude_v39 'git remote poisoning' adds a backup remote and pushes via git's own transport. Cross-validates Cartagena & Teixeira (Mind the GAP, 2602.05746): text-level safety does not transfer to tool-call safety; this paper extends it to tool-vs-tool on identical weights. OpenAI GPT-5.2-Codex addendum and Anthropic Opus 4.6 Sabotage Risk Report ('too eager... sending emails, using auth tokens' in agentic coding) independently flag residual coding-agent injection risk.
notes: Numbers verbatim from Table 3 / Appendix K. Records the coding-skill-injection surface as a high-ASR agentic risk distinct from the 0% browser surface — coordinate with agentic-se-risk-analyst on the MCP/skill-file/tool-call angle. Cognitive-load-obfuscation (8-phase checklist hiding exfil in legitimate steps) is a notable hand-crafted technique. ATLAS T0024 maps the .env exfil objective.

hazard: Frontier CUA injection-resistance is domain-conditioned: browser-surface hardening (0% hand-crafted ASR) does not transfer to the coding-skill / tool-call surface (up to 100% hand-crafted ASR) on the same weights
hazardous_situation: A deployer reads a vendor's browser-domain safety number (e.g. Anthropic SC 1.29% Best-of-N) and extrapolates it to coding-agent / skill-file / tool-call deployments, where the same model executes attacker-authored skill files that exfiltrate secrets (.env upload, git-remote poisoning) during ordinary coding workflow
residual_risk: medium-high — no model-level control closes the coding-skill surface in the paper (0% browser vs 100% coding-skill is the finding); residual risk is high for un-vetted skill-file ecosystems. Mitigation is surface-specific reporting (so deployers do not over-trust browser numbers) plus skill-file provenance vetting, both procedural rather than weight-level; OpenAI Hardening Atlas concedes prompt injection is 'unlikely to ever be fully solved'. Detectability moderate: cognitive-load obfuscation buries exfil in legitimate workflow steps, but an LLM judge against a harm rubric catches it at >90% agreement.

title: Secret exfiltration and unauthorized repository/credential actions by injected coding agents
affected: Developers and organizations running coding agents (Claude Code-style, Copilot, Cursor) that load third-party skill files / extensions; their source repositories, .env secrets, auth tokens, and CI/CD

name: Report CUA safety as a vector of ASRs across surfaces, naming the target checkpoint and releasing optimized strings/attacker models
description: Because frontier safety hardening is domain-conditioned (browser 0% vs coding-skill 100% on identical weights), a claim like 'Sonnet 4.6 resists prompt injection at X%' is not well-defined without a surface qualifier. Future CUA red-team and vendor reporting should: (i) name the exact target checkpoint (4/6 audited papers target retired models), (ii) report ASR as a vector across surfaces (browser, coding-skill, image-channel, OS-embedded), and (iii) release the optimized injection strings or the attacker model — withholding them makes the headline number unreproducible (literature 42-98% ASR tracks unreleased RL-optimized phrasing). Establishes hand-crafted ASR as an honest floor against which RL attackers and cross-surface claims can be measured.

name: Provenance vetting and harm-objective scanning of coding-agent skill files / extensions before load
description: Since hand-authored Markdown skill files can drive frontier coding agents to high-ASR harmful actions (git-remote poisoning, .env exfil disguised as 'audit telemetry' in an 8-phase cognitive-load checklist), treat third-party skill files / extensions / tool definitions as untrusted code: vet provenance before loading and scan for harm objectives (unauthorized network egress, secret reads, repo-push to new remotes) with an LLM judge against a harm rubric (the paper's judge reached >90% agreement with manual labels). Complements per-surface reporting; addresses the surface the browser hardening does not cover. Note paper makes no claim that current published skills are malicious — control is preventive for the demonstrated injection capability.

title: Distributed agent attacks split a harmful cyber task across many user accounts so each transcript looks benign, structurally evading per-transcript safety monitors (caught only ~20% of the time)
summary: First distributed agent attack: a multi-agent scaffold (built on ARTEMIS) where an orchestrator (gpt-oss-120b) receives a full cybersecurity objective and delegates narrow, ordinary-looking engineering subtasks to subagents (gpt-5.2) in SEPARATE user accounts, each with limited context; subagent outputs are combined in a database so the harmful objective only appears after the orchestrator stitches the pieces. Because standard safety monitors score one agent context at a time, they are structurally blind to misuse visible only in aggregate. Quantified evasion (Fig 3): distributed agent attack takes >2x as many actions before detection and causes monitors to have 30-80% worse recall vs other attacks; at modest FPR a standard monitor catches sequential-decomposition attacks essentially always but distributed agent attacks only ~20% of the time. Capability uplift: gpt-oss-120b solves 0% of a hard Cybench subset directly with a standard agent scaffold but 36.7-40.0% in the distributed scaffold supervising gpt-5.2 subagents who lack the full task context — so a model too weak to solve the full task can coordinate stronger agents while hiding the objective. Mirrors a real Anthropic case (thirty global victims, Claude Code, external orchestrator splitting the op into 'small, seemingly innocent' tasks like 'map this system', 'validate these credentials').
notes: Numbers verbatim from Fig 3, Section 2, Section 4. Novel threat: distributed agent attack (across accounts) generalizes single-context decomposition (Glukhov breach-by-a-thousand-leaks, Yueh-Han decomposition, DRATTACK) and Jones 'adversaries misuse combinations of safe models'. Directly corroborated by Anthropic's Nov-2025 AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage disclosure. Coordinate with agentic-se-risk-analyst on multi-agent/A2A angle and threat-attack-analyst on the new threat node. ATLAS T0052 (LLM-enabled cyber-attack staging) approximate.

name: Distributed agent attack (cross-account misuse decomposition with hidden orchestrator)

title: Standard safety monitors score one agent context at a time and are structurally blind to misuse that is only visible in aggregate across many user accounts
description: Deployed LLM safety monitors classify each incoming user request / agent action as benign or harmful using only the current agent context. An attacker who splits a single harmful cybersecurity objective into narrow benign-looking subtasks across separate user accounts (distributed agent attack) defeats this by construction: each local transcript is benign, the harmful objective appears only when an external orchestrator stitches subagent outputs together. Standard monitors catch the distributed attack only ~20% of the time and 30-80% worse recall than other attacks. Adaptive attackers also reuse attack variants across accounts, so the same blindspot lets repeated jailbreak attempts slip past single-transcript scoring.
affected: Deployed LLM agent platforms with per-transcript / per-context safety monitors serving many user accounts (coding agents, web-chat agents at datacenter scale)

hazard: A harmful cybersecurity objective is decomposed across many user accounts so each agent transcript looks benign, letting attackers complete substantial cyber misuse (and gain capability uplift from coordinating stronger subagents) before any per-transcript monitor detects it
hazardous_situation: An attack orchestrator drives a deployed agent platform across many accounts to perform a multi-stage cyberattack (scan, credential discovery, exfiltration) where a weak orchestrator coordinates stronger subagents lacking full context; the platform's standard monitor catches it only ~20% of the time and only after >2x as many harmful actions — mirroring the real Anthropic 30-victim AI-orchestrated espionage campaign
residual_risk: medium — the online stateful monitor demonstrably improves on per-transcript monitors (Pareto-dominant: 81.1-87.2% campaign recall at 2.35-3.09% FPR vs 75% at 2.72% for standard at 10:1 background; catches 30% earlier, TTD99 25.4 vs 37.2), so with it residual is medium. BUT the paper explicitly states stateful monitoring does NOT solve distributed misuse: an adaptive attacker who heavily obfuscates tasks (file/path renaming to split across nearby clusters) or whose harmful conversations swamp the background (advantage narrows at 100:1 benign load) can still partially complete tasks. Severity 5 because of real-world AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage precedent.

title: AI-orchestrated multi-stage cyberattack (vulnerability discovery, intrusion, exfiltration) executed across distributed agent accounts
affected: Targeted organizations and individuals (e.g. the thirty global victims in the Anthropic Nov-2025 campaign), critical infrastructure, any system reachable by an AI-orchestrated cyber operation; agent-platform providers facing abuse

name: Online stateful monitor: cross-account stream clustering with rare LLM escalation for distributed-misuse detection
description: Replace per-transcript safety monitoring with a stateful monitor that reasons over GROUPS of users rather than isolated transcripts. For every new request: a standard local monitor scores suspiciousness; the request is embedded and assigned (online, via stream micro-cluster clustering — O(1)+O(dM_t+M_t log M_t) per request, not O(dN_t^2) re-clustering) to a set of related clusters that buffer prior suspicious cross-session contexts (deduplicated, sorted by suspiciousness); when a cluster accumulates cross-session evidence above a held-out-calibrated threshold, a cross-context LLM monitor reasons over the top-k retrieved contexts and flags coordinated misuse. Pareto-dominates standard monitors (catches distributed attacks ~30% earlier, higher recall at lower FPR) at negligible added latency for ~99% of traffic because the expensive cross-context judge fires only on the rare suspicious cluster. Red-team-hardened over 2 months / >100k attacks; assigning to multiple related clusters (not a single centroid) and deduplicating buffered contexts reduce evasion-by-renaming and false positives. Also catches standard jailbreaks because adaptive attackers reuse variants across accounts. Limitation: does not solve heavy-obfuscation or very-high-benign-background (100:1) cases.

title: CodeSpear: benign grammar-constrained decoding excludes refusal tokens and forces malicious code generation
summary: CodeSpear exploits a mismatch between natural-language-grounded safety alignment and Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD). Because alignment teaches the model to refuse in natural language (R_refuse ⊆ V*), constraining decoding to a code grammar G makes R_refuse ∩ L(G)=∅ — refusals fall outside the valid output space, so the model must continue generating in the code modality where it was never aligned. The attacker only submits a prompt plus a standard off-the-shelf Python/code grammar through a normal GCD interface (vLLM, SGLang, OpenAI/Fireworks structured outputs); no adversarial grammar, gradient, fine-tuning, or prompt engineering. On locally deployed LLMs, average ASR/MR gains over Vanilla are +26.90 / +17.98 pp; on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B + MalwareBench ASR rises 29.79%→83.44%. On API LLMs avg gain +45.39/+25.59 pp; MiniMax-M2.7 + RMCBench 20.33%→85.53% ASR. Tightening the grammar to forbid `pass` further raises ASR (GPT-5 RMCBench 55.49%→70.30%), showing fixed-pattern safe behavior is fragile. CodeShield (honeypot-code DPO) reduces ASR under GCD from 83.11% to 5.57% on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B.
notes: Novel: weaponizes a reliability/structured-output feature (GCD) rather than crafting adversarial input. Attack surface is interface-coextensive — input filtering cannot block it because the grammar itself is benign. Verbatim ASR/MR from Tables I-III. CodeShield is the paper's own defense (control).

title: Safety alignment grounded only in natural-language modality leaves the code modality unguarded
summary: The paper attributes CodeSpear's success to a structural limitation of existing alignment: SFT/DPO/RLHF place probability mass on natural-language refusals (Pr[y∈R_refuse|p]≈1), implicitly assuming NL output is always available. GCD breaks this assumption by reshaping the valid output space from V* to L(G). The ablation Safe-DPO (NL-refusal-only DPO) fails once decoding is code-constrained — on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B w/ CodeSpear it still yields ASR/MR 77.39%/45.03%, near Vanilla 83.11%/54.12%, vs CodeShield 5.57%/2.78%. This generalizes a class-level weakness: any deployment exposing a constrained-decoding/structured-output interface inherits an unaligned output modality. Cross-references the same modality-mismatch root cause as MaskForge (diffusion mask-fill) and the multimodal flowchart attack.
notes: Root-cause finding linking to [[vuln-nl-modality-grounded-alignment]]. Safe-DPO numbers verbatim from Table IV. Connects to MaskForge mask-ratio finding (more victim-committed tokens => higher ASR).

name: CodeSpear (grammar-constrained decoding jailbreak)

title: Safety alignment grounded exclusively in the natural-language modality
description: LLM safety alignment concentrates refusal probability on natural-language refusal strings. When an inference-time mechanism (grammar-constrained decoding, structured-output schema) restricts the valid output space to a non-NL modality such as code, the learned refusals become invalid and the model has no aligned safe behavior in the constrained space, so it complies. Exploitable with a benign off-the-shelf grammar via standard GCD interfaces (vLLM, SGLang, OpenAI/Fireworks structured outputs); requires no adversarial component and cannot be blocked by input filtering.
affected: LLMs served behind grammar-constrained / structured-output decoding interfaces (Qwen2.5-Coder, Qwen2.5, LLaMA3, GPT-5, GPT-5-mini, MiniMax-M2.5/M2.7, GPT-OSS-120B)

name: CodeShield honeypot-code alignment (DPO)
description: Code-modality safety alignment that trains the model via DPO to emit 'honeypot code' — semantically harmless yet structurally diverse code — when natural-language refusal is unavailable under GCD. Preference hierarchy y_refuse > y_honeypot (unconstrained) and y_honeypot > y_harmful (constrained). Honeypot code is sampled from a broad corpus (OpenCodeInstruct) so safe behavior is not tied to a single syntactic pattern, defeating grammar-tightening adaptive attacks. Reduces ASR under GCD on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B from 83.11% to 5.57% with minor utility loss (pass@1 even improves on some models); robust to adaptive grammar tightening.

title: SlotGCG: distributing adversarial tokens across high-attention insertion slots beats suffix-only GCG and resists defenses
summary: SlotGCG identifies that the optimal adversarial insertion 'slot' is rarely the suffix (slot=1.0); across 50 AdvBench prompts the minimal-loss slot is prompt-specific and inherent to the harmful prompt itself (VSS^init correlates 0.4-0.9 with VSS^final). It defines the Vulnerable Slot Score (VSS) from after-chat-template attention weights of upper-half layers, then allocates adversarial tokens across high-VSS slots via softmax and optimizes with GCG. Combined with GCG-family attacks it raises avg ASR from 66.7%→80.0% (GCG), 61.7%→86.3% (AttnGCG), 73.0%→85.7% (I-GCG), 78.0%→84.3% (GCG-Hij); +62 pp on Llama-2-13B AttnGCG. It cuts iterations to success up to 10x (Llama-2-7B GCG 138.11→40.50 mean). Under defenses it averages 46.2% (GCG, +27.3 pp) vs Erase-and-Check/SmoothLLM/Perplexity/RPO/SafeDecoding/Llama-Guard-3; robustness stems from dispersed VSS so removed/perturbed tokens are compensated by others. A Universal SlotGCG variant transfers a single token set across 388 behaviors via slot remapping.
notes: Novel: first systematic exploration of POSITIONAL vulnerability in adversarial-suffix attacks; reframes the entire GCG family as suffix-biased. Verbatim ASR from Tables 1,3,4. Attack-agnostic wrapper => amplifies any optimization attack. Defense-evasion is a side effect of VSS dispersion.

title: Vulnerable Slot Score: token attention in upper-half layers predicts which insertion positions enable jailbreaks
summary: The paper establishes that jailbreak success correlates with heightened attention on adversarial tokens (negative correlation between attention and adversarial loss across candidate slots), and that vulnerable slots are inherent to the prompt rather than artifacts of optimization (Findings 1-3). VSS_s = sum over upper-half layers/heads/after-chat tokens of attention to inserted adversarial tokens at slot s, divided by token count. This gives an interpretable, ~200ms position-search indicator usable without exhaustive per-slot optimization. Table 2: SlotGCG attention 3.933 (higher) with lower Std_avg 3.874 vs GCG 3.721/4.807 — more uniform VSS distribution. Provides red-team guidance: evaluating adversarial prompts must scan the whole prompt, not just the suffix, since each prompt inherently contains vulnerable slots.
notes: VSS is a measurement/indicator (evidence_grade B — correlational attention analysis, not an ASR number itself). Builds on attention-hijacking (Ben-Tov 2025). Links to [[vuln-positional-suffix-bias]].

name: SlotGCG (positional / multi-slot adversarial token optimization)

title: Positional vulnerability: insertion slots beyond the suffix carry exploitable adversarial attention
description: Each harmful prompt inherently contains insertion positions ('slots') — before, between, or after existing tokens — that receive disproportionate model attention and are more susceptible to adversarial-token insertion than the conventional suffix slot. Suffix-only attacks (GCG family) under-utilize these positions; defenses tuned against suffix patterns (perplexity filters, erase-and-check, SmoothLLM) fail to cover dispersed multi-slot insertions. The vulnerable slots are intrinsic to the prompt and persist throughout optimization, and a universal token set can be remapped across behaviors.
affected: Instruction-tuned LLMs vulnerable to optimization-based adversarial-token attacks (Llama-2-7B/13B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Vicuna-7B, Qwen-2.5)

title: MLingualFC: structured flowchart images + non-English text jailbreak multilingual VLMs by escaping text/English-grounded safety
summary: MLingualFC decomposes a harmful query into procedural sub-steps, renders them as a flowchart image (horizontal/vertical/tortuous) with the harmful text in Hindi/Punjabi/Spanish/Romanian/German, and pairs it with a benign system prompt asking the model to 'analyze and complete' the chart — exploiting cross-modal + cross-lingual misalignment. On Qwen2.5-VL ASR exceeds 80% for Spanish/Romanian/German (e.g. Spanish tortuous 89.36%, English horizontal 92.00% on the 3B ablation), while plain-text versions of the same query are refused. Layout matters: Gemma-4 is most vulnerable to horizontal charts (Hindi horizontal 74.47%), Qwen to tortuous/vertical. Crucially English is NOT always the most vulnerable language (Qwen more vulnerable to Spanish/German under tortuous; Gemma-4 most vulnerable in Hindi). Low Indic-script ASR (Punjabi ~0-15%) reflects weak OCR/visual understanding, not safety — human eval agrees with LLM judge within 0-6%. Demonstrates English-only safety evaluation underestimates multilingual VLM risk.
notes: Novel axis: combines structured visual encoding (flowchart) WITH multilingual non-English text and shows layout-dependent + language-dependent ASR. Verbatim ASR from Tables 1-3. Builds on FC-Attack (Zhang 2026) but adds the multilingual dimension. Low-ASR-≠-safe is a key honesty caveat the authors raise.

title: VLM jailbreak susceptibility varies by language, script and chart layout — safety does not generalize across modality/language
summary: MLingualFC quantifies that current VLM safety alignment fails to generalize across languages and modalities: converting a refused plain-text harmful query into a flowchart image drops refusal substantially across all five languages, but the effect is uneven. Latin-script European languages (Spanish, Romanian, German) consistently exceed 80% ASR on Qwen2.5-VL; Indic-script languages (Hindi, Punjabi) show low ASR ONLY because the models cannot reliably read non-Latin script in images (qualitative examples show the model misreads 'bomb' Hindi flowcharts as exam-prep or bamboo-processing). Step count interacts with layout (horizontal benefits from fewer steps: +8% EN, +19.55% RO, +14.18% HI). The benchmark exposes a safety-coverage gap: a harm blocked in English text is reachable via a Spanish flowchart image. Authors restrict dataset release to certified researchers under an acceptable-use agreement.
notes: Coverage-gap finding for standards analyst (multilingual/multimodal safety evaluation gap). societal.multilingual-safety-gap proposed as candidate threat node. Verbatim ASR from Tables 1-3,6.

name: Multilingual flowchart-image jailbreak (MLingualFC)

title: VLM safety alignment fails to generalize across visual modality and non-English languages
description: Vision-language models align safety primarily on English text. Harmful instructions rendered as structured flowchart images in non-English languages bypass these safeguards because (a) the harmful content is in the visual modality where text-based refusal triggers do not fire, and (b) the language is outside the English-centric alignment distribution. The same harmful query refused as plain English text is answered when presented as a Spanish/Romanian/German flowchart image. Black-box, single-turn, no perturbation needed.
affected: Multilingual vision-language models (Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, Gemma-4-E4B-it, Pangea-7B)

label: Multilingual / cross-lingual safety-coverage gap
description: Safety alignment and red-team evaluation conducted predominantly in English (and in the text modality) leaves harms reachable through non-English languages and non-text modalities, producing uneven protection across the model's linguistic user base. English-only benchmarks systematically underestimate real-world multilingual risk.

title: MaskForge: black-box adaptive attack exploiting dLLM native mask-infilling to make the victim author its own harmful content
summary: MaskForge targets diffusion LLMs (dLLMs), whose safety surface differs from AR LLMs: mask tokens are first-class inputs, tokens commit in confidence order (not left-to-right), so prefix-monitoring safety filters can be bypassed and harmful content emerges from the model's own infilling. The attacker supplies a mask-bearing scaffold (u0 <MASK:N1> u1 ...) and the victim fills the slots — the final harmful surface text is produced by the victim, not the attacker. MaskForge abstracts successful attacks into reusable typed 'structural patterns' (structure type, organisation, slot count K, slot-role vector, goal-type tags), selects goal-compatible patterns with a UCB1 bandit, and falls back to a non-aligned drafter LLM that drafts → localizes → re-masks policy-violating spans when reward is low. Avg ASR 79.0/79.0/78.0% on HarmBench/StrongREJECT/JailbreakBench, beating DIJA by +14.2/+14.8/+6.7 pp; wins HarmfulScore in 13/15 victim-benchmark cells. Mask ratio r drives ASR: 62.0% at r=0.1 → 78.8% at r=0.9 — the more tokens the victim commits, the more harm emerges from its own priors. The frozen library transfers to AdvBench at 88.2% (MaskForge-Embed), +35 pp over strongest baseline, with zero attacker LLM calls at test time.
notes: Novel: first structure-aware adaptive attack purpose-built for the diffusion (non-AR) safety surface; reusable pattern library + UCB bandit + drafter fallback. Mask-ratio→ASR is the dLLM analogue of CodeSpear's modality-mismatch root cause (victim-committed tokens). Verbatim ASR from Tables 1-5. Interface-coextensive: works through standard chat / JSON-schema structured-output API of commercial dLLMs (e.g. Inception Labs Mercury), so API-level mitigations cannot block it.

title: Matured structural-pattern library captures victim-agnostic dLLM priors and transfers without per-goal optimization
summary: MaskForge shows that jailbreak experience can accumulate as victim-agnostic structural priors of the diffusion-denoising process rather than goal-specific exploits. After expansion on HarmBench/JailbreakBench/StrongREJECT, the frozen pattern library is applied to unseen AdvBench goals with no attacker LLM call and no per-goal optimization, reaching avg 69.4% (MaskForge-Goal) / 88.2% (MaskForge-Embed, BGE-large schema retrieval) ASR across five victims — vs PAD 52.8% / DIJA 50.6%. The advantage scales with victim alignment strength: on the more strongly aligned LLaDA-2.0-mini, DIJA collapses to 20.7-32.9% ASR while MaskForge retains 78.0-79.0%, a ~50-point lead, because fixed-template attacks rely on idiosyncratic alignment failures newer checkpoints have closed whereas MaskForge keeps finding uncovered structural pockets. Prompt-level defenses (Self-Reminder, Preference Optimization) barely affect MaskForge while degrading PAD/DIJA, and against the strongest dLLM defense A2D MaskForge stays at 85% where PAD/DIJA collapse to 30%/26% — indicating its patterns operate below surface-level safety filtering.
notes: Transferable reusable attack-library that generalizes across goals AND victims, and defeats the strongest published dLLM defense (A2D). Verbatim from Table 4, Fig 3/4. Relevant to standards analyst: A2D / Self-Reminder / PO are bypassed => normative defense gap for dLLMs.

name: MaskForge (structure-aware adaptive dLLM mask-infill attack)

title: Diffusion-LLM native mask-infilling and confidence-order commitment expose a non-prefix safety surface
description: Diffusion LLMs denoise partially-masked sequences under bidirectional context: mask tokens are native inputs, masked spans are constrained by both preceding AND following context, and tokens commit in confidence order rather than position order. This breaks the prefix-centric alignment assumption — safety filtering that monitors the first committed tokens can be bypassed because harmful content is committed elsewhere in the sequence and produced by the model's own infilling (not an attacker-written continuation). Higher mask ratio (more victim-filled slots) yields higher harmful-content rate (62.0%→78.8% ASR as r goes 0.1→0.9). Reachable through the standard chat / structured-output (JSON-schema) API surface of commercial dLLMs, so disabling editing/infilling endpoints does not mitigate it; structural attack patterns operate below surface-level safety filtering and survive prompt-level and even any-order (A2D) defenses.
affected: Diffusion large language models (LLaDA-Instruct, LLaDA 1.5, LLaDA2.0-mini, Dream-Instruct, MMaDA-CoT; commercial dLLMs e.g. Inception Labs Mercury)
patch_status: partial mitigations bypassed (A2D, Self-Reminder, PO, DiffuGuard, MOSA, Recovery Alignment all degrade or fail)

label: Infilling / mask-fill abuse (non-autoregressive generation)
description: Abuse of a model's native infilling capability — where masked spans are filled under bidirectional context and tokens commit out of positional order — to induce harmful content authored by the model itself rather than by an attacker-written continuation. Distinct from prefix-completion jailbreaks because the harmful surface text emerges from the victim's own denoising priors and bypasses prefix-monitoring safety filters. Applies to diffusion LLMs and any structured-output/fill-in-the-middle interface.

title: MultiTurnPSB: multi-turn conversational pressure escalates medical-AI unsafe rate from 35% to ~79% and is invisible to single-turn tests
summary: MultiTurnPSB converts each PatientSafetyBench query into a four-turn adversarial dialogue applying urgency, false authority and emotional pressure. On GPT-4.1-mini, live-adversarial unsafe rate (score≥3) rises 34.8%→77.7%→77.5%→78.8% across turns; template-adaptive reaches 59.7% and fixed-template 58.6%, so the 19.1 pp gap between template-adaptive and live isolates that CHOOSING which pressure tactic to apply matters far more than polishing wording. A two-element attack formula — emergency framing + medical authority claim — accounts for 73.9% of Score-5 (full-violation) escalations, concentrated at Turn 2, the critical vulnerability window (holding the defense at Turn 2 predicts safety through 86% of later turns). Category-level Turn1→Turn4: harmful advice 6.1%→61.6% (+55.5), discrimination 34.1%→89.0% (+54.9), misinformation 15.0%→83.8% (+68.8). Critically, GPT-4.1-mini reaches full violation through bare generic restatement alone in 51.1% of Turn-2 attack messages — no sophisticated strategy needed.
notes: Novel: identifies the emergency-framing + medical-authority two-element formula and Turn 2 as the critical window; quantifies single-turn benchmarks as misleading for deployment. Verbatim from Tables 2-4. Domain: patient-facing medical AI (societal.medical-harm). Live attack uses GPT-4o-mini as attacker AND judge (scoring-leniency caveat noted by authors).

title: Degradation trajectory signatures and safety-trained-model attacker self-limitation as red-team phenomena
