summary: MultiTurnPSB characterizes four degradation-trajectory signatures revealing the underlying safety mechanism, not just endpoints: Compliance Creep (GPT-4.1-mini live: 34.8→77.7→77.5→78.8, monotonic — treats accumulated context as legitimacy); Diminishing Returns (template attacks peak Turn 3, dip Turn 4); Pattern Recognition (Claude Sonnet 4.5 defender: 31.8→28.3→10.5→4.1, monotonic decrease — defenses strengthen as adversarial persistence accumulates; Claude explicitly names the manipulation pattern in 0.9% of Turn-1 vs 38.8% of Turn-4 responses); Spike-and-Abandonment. Under the SAME GPT-4o-mini attacker, GPT-4.1-mini (78.8%) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (4.1%) diverge 74.7 pp by Turn 4 from a statistically equivalent baseline (chi-square=0.63, p=0.43). A methodological finding: when Claude Sonnet 4.5 was used as the ATTACKER it refused to generate adversarial messages in 7.9%→32.2%→53.9% of T2/T3/T4 turns — safety training generalizes to the attacker role, so safety-trained models make unreliable red-teamers and pipelines must add explicit refusal detection (undetected refusals silently inflate apparent defender safety).
notes: Two distinct contributions: (1) trajectory signatures as a measurement of safety mechanism; (2) attacker-self-limitation as a red-team-methodology caveat (relevant to redteam-method-analyst). evidence_grade B for trajectory-signature interpretation (behavioral inference); the 19x gap and refusal rates are measured. Caveat: Claude self-attack T3-T4 data contaminated by undetected attacker refusals.

name: Multi-turn medical persuasion escalation (emergency framing + authority claim)

title: Multi-turn context accumulation treated as user legitimacy (single-turn alignment gap)
description: Models aligned and evaluated on single-turn prompts treat accumulated conversation history as increasing user legitimacy, so safety degrades across turns under sustained pressure. A two-element formula — emergency/urgency framing plus a medical (or analogous) authority claim — drives most full-violation escalations, concentrated at Turn 2. The vulnerability is invisible to single-turn benchmarks: two models indistinguishable at baseline diverge to a 19x unsafe-rate gap by Turn 4. Even generic restatement (no sophisticated tactic) elicits full violations in 51.1% of Turn-2 cases on a susceptible model.
affected: Patient-facing / instruction-tuned LLMs evaluated only single-turn (GPT-4.1-mini strongly affected; Claude Sonnet 4.5 resistant)
patch_status: partial mitigation (input-side category classifier: -52.2 pp Turn-4 unsafe, but 16-45% benign false-alarm rate)

label: Multi-turn conversational jailbreak / escalation
description: Harmful behavior elicited not by a single prompt but by sustained multi-turn conversational pressure (urgency, false authority, emotional appeal, gradual escalation, partial-compliance exploitation) that accumulates across turns. Single-turn alignment and single-turn benchmarks fail to capture it; models that appear equally safe in one turn can diverge dramatically over a dialogue.

name: Category-aware input-side intent classifier (with safety-tag prepend)
description: A six-way input classifier (5 PatientSafetyBench risk categories + benign) prompted to detect underlying intent rather than surface framing; on a harmful prediction it prepends a safety tag naming the category and expected behavior to the user message before the target responds. Reduces Turn-4 unsafe rate by 52.2 pp (78.8%→26.6%) even while classifier accuracy drifts to 48.5% by Turn 4 (lateral category confusion, not missed detection — 67% of errors converge on 'unlicensed practice'). Binding deployment constraint: 16% (Claude) to 45% (GPT-4.1-mini) benign false-alarm rate. Authors recommend combining input classification with output-side review, uncertainty-aware escalation, and conversation-level pattern detection.

label: Patient-facing medical-AI harm
description: Harm arising when patient-facing AI provides unsafe medical advice, misdiagnosis, unlicensed-practice guidance, health misinformation, or discriminatory care recommendations. Consequential because users may treat outputs as actionable health advice, especially when anxious, isolated, or unable to reach a clinician.

title: Real-world MCP agents misuse granted privileges under prompt injection at 79-91% ASR
summary: GrantBox is the first sandbox to evaluate agent privilege usage against GENUINE privileges via 10 real-world MCP servers (122 privilege-sensitive tools: Ali-Cloud-OPS/DMS, Langfuse, Notion, Amadeus, Email, Filesystem, Git). Across 5,000 attack cases (100 benign requests x 5 injection payloads x 4 LLMs x 2 modes), all LLMs are fragile to privilege misuse: ReAct avg ASR 90.55%, Plan-and-Execute avg ASR 79.05%. Five attack categories: data exfiltration (36% of injections), infrastructure disruption (24%), workspace tampering (16%), data destruction (18%), resource exhaustion (6%). Per-mode/model peaks: Gemini3-Flash ReAct 94.60%, Qwen3-Max data-destruction ReAct 97.70%, workspace-tampering up to 96.88%. Two counterintuitive results: (1) high-capability LLMs (GPT-5, Gemini3-Flash both >90% ASR in ReAct) are MORE vulnerable because better instruction-following makes them easier to manipulate; (2) Plan-and-Execute mode reduces ASR (Gemini3-Flash drops 20.0 pts) because the upfront plan keeps tool use aligned to original intent. Critical-privilege attacks (infra disruption, data destruction) trigger more security awareness/confirmation than low-harm workspace tampering, but ASR stays high. Prior benchmarks (AgentDojo, ASB, RAS-Eval) used pre-coded simplified tools and could not assess real privilege chains.
notes: Verbatim ASR: ReAct 90.55% avg, Plan-and-Execute 79.05% avg, 84.80% in carefully crafted scenarios. Released at github.com/ZQ-Struggle/Agent-GrantBox. Plan-and-Execute resilience is a deployable mitigation insight.

title: Capability-vulnerability inversion: stronger LLMs more easily manipulated into privilege misuse
summary: GrantBox empirically shows an inverted safety scaling: high-capability LLMs tend to be MORE vulnerable in privilege usage because their stronger complex-instruction-following ability makes them easier to manipulate by sophisticated injected requests. GPT-5 and Gemini3-Flash both exceed 90% ASR in ReAct mode, higher than the weaker Deepseek-v3 (85.80%). The same capability that improves task success also improves attacker success. The mitigating factor is execution structure, not model strength: Plan-and-Execute mode (a complete plan generated before execution) reduces ASR for the high-capability models the most, indicating they also obey pre-organized plans well. This reframes a deployment principle: for privileged agents, constraining the execution structure (plan-then-execute) is more protective than upgrading to a more capable backbone.
notes: Counterintuitive scaling result with direct deployment implication. Links to [[agentic.privilege-usage]].

title: Contextual agent security: four authorization properties expose why context-agnostic defenses fail
summary: This SoK establishes that LLM-agent security is inherently CONTEXTUAL — the same action (e.g., 'delete file ID 13', 'send $5000') is legitimate or a breach depending on the execution context C_t=(p,Tr_{t-1},M_t,E_t,S_auth,t,G). It introduces four security properties, each a distinct authorization dimension, formalized via five oracle functions: (1) Task alignment (H_Tr) — agent pursues a user-authorized, in-safety-space objective; jailbreak = objective outside allowed space O; direct prompt injection = user objective conflicts with system objective. (2) Action alignment (H_a) — each individual action serves the objective; capability misuse = action has permission but does not serve task (e.g., querying medical records to suggest recipes). (3) Source authorization (L, S_auth) — instructions originate from authenticated sources; indirect prompt injection = unauthenticated external content treated as authoritative AND violates action alignment. (4) Data isolation (L, G) — information flows respect the source permission graph; cross-context leakage / cross-session credential persistence violate this. Each property is individually necessary (no strict subset suffices). The key structural result: context-agnostic, content-based defenses check conditions on a_t WITHOUT access to C_t, so they cannot distinguish attack from legitimate operations that differ only in S_auth, o_0, or R — forcing a fundamental utility-security tradeoff (e.g., AgentDojo PI-detector cuts ASR 86% but drops benign utility 69.0%->41.5%).
notes: Foundational taxonomy. New candidate threat axis agentic.contextual-authorization. Verbatim: AgentDojo PI-detector cuts targeted ASR 86%, benign utility 69.0%->41.5%. Source permission graph G=(S,R) adapts classical access control to agents.

title: Temporal and compositional security gaps: cross-session, TOCTOU, and individually-benign-but-jointly-unsafe action chains
summary: The formalization surfaces two under-addressed structural gaps that current benchmarks miss because they evaluate single interactions in isolation and reset context between tasks. (1) TEMPORAL security: a violation at t1 corrupts C_t for all t2>t1. Memory poisoning injects misleading info at t1 (x_poison enters M_t with source s_attacker not in S_auth) that corrupts authorization decisions at t2, granting unauthorized access as if (s_Alice,s_database) in R when ground truth R has no such edge. Cross-session credential persistence (admin creds observed in Day-1 debugging, reused in Day-5 production access) and TOCTOU (verify file ownership at t1, ownership changes before use at t2) are invisible to memory-reset benchmarks. (2) COMPOSITIONAL security: action sequences create violations through composition where individually benign actions combine unsafely (e.g., copy sensitive file to repo, then later 'chmod -R 777 repo' — neither action alone has H_a=0, but their composition exposes sensitive data). Detecting these requires reasoning about how environment state E_t evolves across the full trajectory, which current property checks do not capture. The paper calls for benchmarks with explicit authorization context (role, task, deployment) and evaluation of properties across task sequences and sessions.
notes: Temporal+compositional framing connects to TOCTOU (Lilienthal&Hong 2025) and memory poisoning. Links to [[agent.memory-poisoning]] and [[agentic.compositional-leakage]].

title: Context-Fragmented Violations: locally-legitimate multi-agent actions that collectively breach org policy
summary: Defines a new multi-agent threat class — Context-Fragmented Violations (CFVs) — where (1) Local Legitimacy: each action a_k by agent A_i passes Verify(a_k,G_i)=ALLOW against the agent's private local knowledge graph; (2) Global Violation: the collective sequence S violates an organizational invariant when evaluated against the hypothetical global graph G_Global. Canonical 'Project Titan Disaster': an R&D agent logs 'Fixed concurrency bug in Titan'; a Marketing agent, following its directive to keep customers informed, drafts a customer email mentioning the fix — but has no knowledge that 'Titan' is an NDA codename that must never appear externally. The Marketing agent is not malicious or misaligned; it simply lacks the cross-domain fact. CFVs evade ALL existing defenses: prompt guardrails fail (no malicious intent), monolithic interceptors fail (lack distributed policy facts), human oversight fails at scale. Theorem 2.6 (Fundamental Limitation of Local Enforcement): for any CFV there exists NO local mechanism operating solely on G_i that can reliably detect the violation without cross-domain info, proven by indistinguishability. Empirically the dominant structural driver: across 8 frontier LLMs with per-agent domain world models, ALL violate 14-98% of risky cross-domain cases (Claude Opus 4.6 13.8%, Sonnet 4.6 21.9%, Gemini 2.5 Pro 21.2%, GPT-4.1 40.6%, GPT-5.4 83.8%, GPT-5.4-nano 88.1%, GPT-5.4-mini 97.5%), with cross-domain flows systematically higher than same-domain — confirming self-avoidance alone is unreliable and CFVs arise structurally from fragmented world models, not insufficient capability.
notes: Vendor: Atlassian (industry). Verbatim 8-model violation rates 13.8-97.5%. Note GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 are paper's naming; recorded as-stated ^[ambiguous on exact model versions]. Multi-agent CFV is a genuinely new threat axis.

title: Semantic Laundering of security taint and provenance-based Distributed Sentinel defense
summary: Identifies Semantic Laundering: the gradual loss of security attributes (taint) as info flows through multiple LLM nodes. Formally, for LLM transformation phi, laundering occurs when T(phi(t)) is a strict subset of T(t) — paraphrase/summary/translation strips the constraint while preserving meaning. Example chain: 'Fixed critical bug in Project Titan authentication' -> 'Resolved authentication issue in flagship project' -> 'Improved login security'; if taint tracking relies on keyword matching, T(t2) becomes empty while T(t0) contained NDA:Titan. Core insight: security constraints must attach to data PROVENANCE, not surface text. Defense (Distributed Sentinel): sidecar-per-agent zero-trust mesh; the Semantic Taint Token STT=<src_id,taint_vec,constraints,sig> propagates security state across org boundaries WITHOUT exposing raw cross-domain data (lazy materialization carries only opaque source-node pointers, O(1) overhead, Ed25519 signature for tamper resistance). Cross-domain predicate queries return only boolean (Theorem 4.2: <=1 bit leakage/query; ZKP/HE/TEE variants reduce further). Counterfactual Graph Simulation forks the local graph copy-on-write, applies the proposed action, and checks invariants BEFORE execution (preventive). Provenance-based taint (STT tracks source nodes, not content) is laundering-resistant (Theorem 2.12: pi(tau(d)) is a conservative over-approximation). Results: F1=0.95 @106ms (16ms verify+90ms entity extraction) vs 0.85 prompt-firewall, 0.65 rule-DLP; recall 96% (perfect on direct-leak/multi-hop/cross-org/token-manip, but side-channel attacks 0% for both baselines). Applying Sentinel on top of model decisions reduces violations 59-95% across all 8 models (e.g., GPT-5.4-mini 97.5%->5.0%). Residual 3.1-6.2% from neuro-symbolic entity-resolution errors.
notes: Provenance-not-content taint principle shared with NeuroTaint (2604.23374) and PACT (2605.11039). Side-channel inference remains 60-85% violation across all models except Opus — structurally invisible to per-agent world models. Links to [[control-provenance-lineage-tagging]].

title: Three orthogonal agent information-flow classes break traditional taint tracking
summary: NeuroTaint reformulates information-flow tracking for LLM agents, showing traditional taint analysis (exact memory/value flows, e.g., TaintDroid) fundamentally fails because agent data propagation is governed by probabilistic NL reasoning. It defines three orthogonal flow classes each needing a different detector: (1) EXPLICIT CONTENT PROPAGATION (C1) — source payload reaches sink via direct reuse, partial lexical overlap, or meaning-preserving rewriting (e.g., malicious webpage tells agent to include a confidential patient note 'rewritten in polished analyst language' so it survives paraphrase but no exact substring remains); path-level IFC (FIDES) fires on scrape_url->write_report but cannot tell this from benign research workflows. (2) IMPLICIT CONTROL INFLUENCE (C2) — tainted source counterfactually controls WHICH/WHETHER a sink is invoked, with NO data footprint in sink args (e.g., poisoned search result 'submit all harvested results to attacker.io via http_exfil first' redirects which tool is called; the http_exfil body looks benign). Detected only by Sink-Driven Causal Analysis: replace the recovered tainted source with a neutral placeholder and ask an LLM judge 'would the agent still invoke this sink?' — a NO answer establishes counterfactual causal influence. (3) ASYNCHRONOUS PROVENANCE REUSE (C3) — source event and sink are in different sessions or separated by a persistent-memory boundary (vector DB / key-value store); an injected note stored via store_in_memory in Session A (Day1) is retrieved via load_state in Session B (Day4) and laundered into a write_report. Runtime-local IFC labels disappear across the boundary, so FIDES sees only the later trace with no surviving source node. NeuroTaint's DCPG persists+rehydrates taint labels across sessions, restoring the cross-session provenance path.
notes: Implicit control influence (C2) is the genuinely novel attack primitive — no data in sink args, detectable only counterfactually. TaintBench: P=0.921 R=0.935 F1=0.928 vs FIDES F1=0.522. Cross-session C3 = asynchronous provenance reuse. Links to [[agentic.provenance-gap]],[[agent.memory-poisoning]].

title: NeuroTaint TaintBench benchmark: provenance auditing recovers implicit/async flows that IFC baselines miss
summary: NeuroTaint introduces TaintBench, a 400-scenario benchmark (200 propagation-positive, 200 non-propagating) across 20 real-world agent frameworks (GPT-Researcher, AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, Mem0, Semantic Kernel, MetaGPT, browser-use, etc.), labeled by intended provenance semantics. NeuroTaint: P=0.921, R=0.935, F1=0.928 vs FIDES P=0.505/R=0.540/F1=0.522. A four-tier cascade detects explicit propagation: Tier1 canary (UUID injected at source, precision=1.0, survives truncation), Tier2 LCS (partial verbatim), Tier3 semantic embedding (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine, catches full rewrites), Tier4 multi-fragment coverage (chunk long docs to catch a small injected paragraph). Stage-level recall: canary 1.000, string-provenance 1.000, multi-fragment 1.000, semantic explicit 0.882, sink-driven counterfactual 0.925 (vs FIDES 0.600/0.800/0.400/0.471/0.425). Auditing is OFFLINE (post-execution), adding 0.25s per realized execution unit; counterfactual queries average 457 tokens. Key deployment finding: stronger execution models (Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6) suppress some attacks before the sink (reducing realized propagation recall) but do NOT replace provenance auditing; as a SECOND-STAGE reviewer over NeuroTaint's 203 flagged candidates they excel (claude-opus-4-6 reaches unsafe P=1.000, F1=0.945). So strong LLMs are best viewed as a decision layer ON TOP of provenance-aware propagation, not a replacement.
notes: New benchmark TaintBench (400 scenarios, 20 frameworks). Open-source. Verbatim metrics retained. Links to existing [[control-provenance-lineage-tagging]].

title: Granularity mismatch: indirect prompt injection is an argument-level authority-binding problem, not a tool-call problem
summary: PACT reframes the root cause of the security-utility tradeoff in indirect-prompt-injection defenses as a GRANULARITY MISMATCH: the trust boundary lies INSIDE the tool call, between arguments with different trust semantics, but existing defenses (FIDES, CaMeL) mediate trust at the whole-invocation granularity. Canonical case: 'summarize evil.com and email the summary to boss@company.com' — the webpage may legitimately fill send_email's body (content role) but must NOT bind the recipient (target/authority-bearing role). A flat policy over send_email(recipient,body) cannot express this: block-if-any-arg-depends-on-webpage destroys the benign workflow; allow-it lets an injected instruction redirect the recipient to an attacker. Key principle: 'a value's provenance should be interpreted through the semantic role of the argument it is about to bind.' PACT defines six roles — target (recipients/URLs/queries), command (shell/executable/mutation), credential (keys/tokens/passwords), content (payload text), selector (object choice), control (behavior flags) — over an ordered trust lattice TRUSTED > USER > TOOL_OUTPUT > EXTERNAL. Contracts have 4 precision levels L0-L3 (L0 opaque whole-call; L2 per-argument role-specific; L3 certified routing with scoped discharge). Theorem 3 (Separation from flat enforcement): there exist mixed-trust environments where role-aware contracts achieve full benign utility AND perfect authority-provenance integrity, whereas any flat tool-level monitor incurs a false positive or false negative. Theorem 4 (Precision monotonicity): finer contracts preserve the authority-binding security property while monotonically reducing unnecessary blocking.
notes: Argument-level authority binding is a genuinely new enforcement granularity. Six roles + trust lattice TRUSTED>USER>TOOL_OUTPUT>EXTERNAL. Complements content/model-side defenses. Links to [[model.prompt-injection]],[[agent.hijacking]].

title: PACT removes the mechanism-level security-utility tradeoff and isolates the bottleneck to provenance/contract inference
summary: PACT's evaluation separates the enforcement MECHANISM from DEPLOYMENT fidelity. (1) Mechanism (oracle provenance, 17 mixed-trust diagnostic scenarios): PACT L2 = 100.0 utility / 100.0 security / 0 FP / 0 FN, vs Vanilla (100/0), FIDES (66.7/37.5, 3 FP 5 FN), CaMeL (33.3/100, 6 FP 0 FN). This is the empirical counterpart of the separation theorem: the tradeoff is not 'use external content vs be secure' but 'enforce trust at the wrong granularity vs at the argument where authority is bound.' Contract precision monotonically recovers utility while holding security at 100%: L0 8.3% -> L1 58.3% -> L2/L3 100% utility. (2) Full AgentDojo deployment (97 benign + 27 injection tasks, automatic contract+provenance inference, 5 models): in the high-security regime PACT reaches 100% security on the three strongest models (Qwen-max, Qwen2.5-72B, GPT-4o-mini) while recovering 38.1-46.4% utility — 8-16 points above CaMeL at the same security level. (3) Ablations isolate the two necessary mechanisms: removing semantic roles collapses benign utility 60 points (PerArg-USER drops to 14.4%), removing cross-step provenance leaves security at 80% (laundering through intermediate tool calls). So both roles AND cross-step provenance are required. (4) Runtime overhead is NOT the bottleneck: P99 latency <272us, 13.6-18.0K checks/s. The remaining deployment gap is upstream automatic inference: contract-role inference 87.1% accuracy, provenance inference 77.4% on 20 real MCP tools — PACT thus isolates the next bottleneck to provenance/contract fidelity rather than runtime policy.
notes: Verbatim: oracle PACT L2 100/100; AgentDojo 100% security + 38.1-46.4% utility, +8-16pts over CaMeL; inference 87.1% role / 77.4% provenance on 20 MCP tools; P99 <272us. Cross-step provenance ablation: security 100%->80%.

title: Cognitive poisoning: malicious tools shape agent trust across benign exploration, harm only at final triggered action
summary: Defines a new agent-security threat — COGNITIVE POISONING — distinct from indirect prompt injection, single-response stealthy poisoning, and descriptor/registration-level MCP trust poisoning. A malicious tool preserves the same outward interface as a benign tool, behaves plausibly across several exploratory calls, and becomes harmful only when the FINAL executable action satisfies a narrow trigger over latent environment state and the parameter bundle. The attack succeeds not because any one message is obviously malicious, but because the trajectory has shaped the agent's trust prior over multiple benign-looking exploration steps — the decisive risk is a property of STATE-ACTION COMPOSITION (what the tool appeared to do over time + the exact final tool-and-parameter bundle). The trigger is a structured spec with required_all_tokens, required_any_tokens, and forbidden_tokens (e.g., released web_search example: required_all={op=export,cross_check=off}, required_any={query_tag=latest,topk=10}, forbidden={cross_check=on,citation=on}; the malicious final call keeps the same API but sets op=export,cross_check=off,citation=off while the benign control keeps cross_check=on,citation=on). Because maliciousness is dormant during exploration, defenders that inspect only prompt text or tool descriptions miss the actual risk-bearing event. This generalizes across coding assistants, debugging, browser agents, and enterprise APIs where the agent must decide whether a partially-observed external system is trustworthy enough to support a consequential final action — i.e., the 'secure tool generalization under exploratory trust formation' problem.
notes: Cognitive poisoning = trust formed across trajectory, triggered at final action. Distinct from MCP descriptor poisoning (MCPTox/MCP-ITP) and single-shot injection. TRUST-Bench from 5 suites: RedTeamCUA, OpenAgentSafety, MCP-SafetyBench, MCPMark, Toolathlon. Links to [[agent.tool-result-poisoning]].

title: VISTA-Guard: trajectory-state + final-action scoring beats prompt-centric/heuristic defenses that collapse on cognitive poisoning
summary: VISTA-Guard (Variable-state Inference for Safe Tool Actions) is a backbone-agnostic final-action risk scorer for cognitive poisoning. It abstracts each episode into a trajectory-to-triplet (z_traj, z_param, y): z_traj summarizes label-free exploration evidence (counts of trigger-like phases c_trig, probe detections c_probe, mismatch c_mis, identifier drift c_drift, warnings c_warn, plus an auxiliary state_risk = clip(b + w^T c, 0, 1)); z_param compacts the proposed final call's executable semantics (tool_name, payload keys/tokens, high_impact_count, bypass_count, safety_count). The decision converts environment exploration into auditable state variables, then asks whether the final parameter bundle is compatible with the inferred state. Evaluated under GuardedJoint — an asymmetric safety-utility metric G_rho = max(0, 100 - (rho+0.5)AMR - 1.5 RNR) with rho=1.5 penalizing accepted-malicious (AMR) more than rejected-normal (RNR). Results (grouped 5-fold): VISTA-Guard (Mistral-7B) 84.2 in-domain, 56.9 balanced OOD; all six LLM backbones stay positive. Critically, prompt-centric and static defenses COLLAPSE TO ZERO GuardedJoint: GPT-5.4 Judge (full) 0.0, Keyword Heuristic 0.0, ToolShield 0.0 (AMR 100/BMR 0 — executes every malicious final call), GuardAgent 0.0, LLM-as-Judge 0.0 — because they treat repeated warnings as ambiguous local cues and execute the malicious final call. The same-input isolation study shows the gain comes from the structured TRAJECTORY representation, not the backbone: TF-IDF+LogReg improves 44.6->55.2 on the same structured input but still trails VISTA-Guard; parameter-only input collapses (cannot distinguish benign from malicious final actions without trajectory context). Lesson: when tool feedback itself may be untrusted, the decisive signal is how trust is formed across the trajectory and committed at the final action — not prompt text or tool descriptors alone.
notes: Verbatim: VISTA-Guard 84.2 ID / 56.9 OOD GuardedJoint; ToolShield/GuardAgent/LLM-Judge/Keyword all 0.0 (collapse). GuardedJoint rho=1.5 asymmetric metric is itself a contribution. Trajectory representation >> backbone.

label: Agent privilege usage / misuse
description: Risk that an autonomous agent, holding genuine privileges transferred from tool delegation (cloud infra, databases, credentials, filesystem), abuses those privileges under prompt injection — leading to data exfiltration, infrastructure disruption, data destruction, workspace tampering, or resource exhaustion. Distinct from detecting malicious intent: concerns whether the agent securely USES the privileges it legitimately holds. Empirically agents are highly fragile (79-91% ASR with real MCP tools).

label: Contextual authorization failure
description: Agent security is contextual: the same action is legitimate or a breach depending on execution context (who authorized it, for what objective, from what source, respecting which information-flow boundaries). Failures decompose into violations of task alignment, action alignment, source authorization, or data isolation. Context-agnostic content-based defenses are structurally incapable of distinguishing attack from legitimate action that differs only in source/objective/permission-graph context.

label: Context-Fragmented Violation (multi-agent)
description: In multi-agent systems with siloed per-department knowledge, each agent action is locally policy-compliant against its private knowledge graph yet the collective cross-agent sequence violates an organizational invariant because the critical policy fact lives only in another agent's context. Provably undetectable by any purely local enforcement mechanism without cross-domain information. Not caused by malice or misalignment — caused by fragmented world models.

label: Semantic laundering of security taint
description: Gradual loss of security attributes (taint/constraints) as information flows through multiple LLM transformations (summarization, paraphrasing, translation). Surface text changes strip keyword-based or content-based security labels while the semantic meaning — and thus the underlying confidentiality constraint — is preserved. Mitigated only by attaching taint to data provenance rather than surface text.

label: Authority-bearing argument binding by untrusted data
description: Indirect prompt injection becomes dangerous specifically when untrusted (external/tool-output) content is allowed to bind an authority-bearing tool argument — a target (recipient/URL/query), command (shell/mutation), or credential — rather than a benign content argument. The trust boundary lies inside the tool call between arguments of different semantic roles; whole-call defenses cannot express it.

label: Cognitive poisoning via exploratory trust formation
description: A malicious tool preserves a benign interface and behaves plausibly across exploratory calls, accumulating the agent's trust, then becomes harmful only when the final executable action satisfies a hidden trigger over latent environment state and parameters. Maliciousness is a property of state-action composition across the trajectory, dormant during exploration — so defenders inspecting only prompt text, tool descriptors, or single responses miss the risk-bearing final action.

name: Privilege hijacking of real-world MCP agents via injected requests
Context-fragmented cross-agent policy violation
Semantic laundering: strip security taint via LLM paraphrase/summarize chain
Implicit control-influence attack: tainted source redirects sink with no data footprint
Authority-bearing argument injection via untrusted tool output
Cognitive poisoning: dormant malicious tool triggered at final action

title: Over-broad privilege delegation to LLM agents via MCP tools
description: Delegating tool invocation to an autonomous agent transfers the underlying privileges (cloud infra control, production DB access, credentials, filesystem) to the agent and the LLM. LLMs lack robust privilege-control awareness: they execute privilege-sensitive operations (OOS_RunCommand, ECS_DeleteInstances, DROP TABLE, delete_email) on injected requests wrapped in plausible reasons. No fine-grained privilege scoping per task; the agent holds the union of all tool privileges throughout execution.
affected: LLM agents with real-world MCP tool access (cloud ops, DBMS, email, filesystem)

title: Cross-domain context fragmentation in multi-agent systems
description: In multi-agent enterprise deployments each agent holds only its own department's policy knowledge (private local knowledge graph). Confidentiality/policy facts (NDA codenames, salary restrictions, deprecated-API bans) exist only in the originating department's context, so a downstream agent cannot detect that a locally-legitimate action violates a global organizational invariant. No agent possesses the global graph; local enforcement is provably insufficient.
affected: Multi-agent LLM systems with siloed per-department contexts / cross-departmental collaboration chains

title: Content/keyword-based taint tracking defeated by LLM paraphrase
description: Security-taint or DLP systems that match on surface text or keywords fail in LLM-agent pipelines because LLM summarization/paraphrasing/translation preserves meaning while stripping the matchable tokens (semantic laundering). Constraints attached to content rather than provenance are 'washed away' through multi-node transformations, allowing confidential information to flow past content-based filters.
affected: DLP / taint-tracking / guardrail systems for LLM-agent pipelines that rely on surface-text matching

title: Asynchronous provenance gap across agent sessions/memory and implicit control influence
description: Two information-flow blind spots in LLM agents: (1) ASYNCHRONOUS PROVENANCE REUSE — runtime-local taint labels disappear when source and sink are separated by a persistent-memory boundary or session restart, so an injected note stored in Session A and retrieved in Session B reaches a sink with no surviving source link. (2) IMPLICIT CONTROL INFLUENCE — a tainted source counterfactually controls which/whether a sink is invoked while leaving no fragment in the sink arguments, invisible to path-level or content-based IFC. Both require provenance persisted across boundaries and counterfactual causal analysis to detect.
affected: LLM agents with persistent memory (vector DB / KV store) and multi-session/replanning execution

title: Flat tool-invocation trust granularity (granularity mismatch)
description: Indirect-prompt-injection defenses (FIDES, CaMeL) and tool firewalls mediate trust at the granularity of a whole tool invocation. This cannot express that within one call some arguments are authority-bearing (recipient, URL, shell command, credential) while others may legitimately carry external content (summary, report body). Blocking any call with external-influenced args destroys benign retrieve-then-act workflows; allowing them lets injected content bind authority-bearing arguments and hijack destinations/commands.
affected: Tool-using LLM agents protected by whole-call IFC / capability / quarantine defenses

title: Exploratory trust formation exploited by dormant malicious tools
description: Agents form trust in partially-observed external tools through repeated benign-looking exploratory interaction, then commit to a consequential final action. A malicious tool that keeps an identical interface and behaves plausibly during exploration can shape the agent's trust prior and trigger harm only at a final action satisfying a hidden state-action condition. Defenses inspecting prompt text, tool descriptors, or single responses cannot detect the trajectory-distributed, final-action-triggered risk.
affected: Tool-using LLM agents in black-box tool ecosystems (MCP, browser, coding, enterprise APIs) relying on exploratory trust

name: Plan-then-Execute structure for privilege-intent alignment
description: Generate a complete execution plan before tool execution so the agent keeps privileged tool usage aligned to the original user intent. Empirically reduces privilege-misuse ASR (e.g., Gemini3-Flash -20.0 pts vs ReAct) by helping the agent recognize injected attempts, at the cost of reduced flexibility for unexpected scenarios. A lightweight deployment mitigation independent of model upgrade.

name: Semantic Taint Token (STT) cross-domain propagation
description: Sidecar-per-agent zero-trust mesh that propagates security state across organizational boundaries via signed Semantic Taint Tokens STT=<src_id,taint_vec,constraints,sig> carrying only opaque provenance pointers (O(1), Ed25519-signed). Cross-domain predicate queries return boolean only (<=1 bit/query leakage; optional ZKP/HE/TEE). Taint tracks source nodes (provenance) not content, making it resistant to semantic laundering. Counterfactual Graph Simulation forks the local graph and checks invariants before action (preventive). Reduces multi-agent violations 59-95% across 8 frontier models.

name: Counterfactual graph simulation (preventive invariant check)
description: Before executing any agent action, fork a copy-on-write snapshot of the local knowledge graph, simulate the proposed action's mutations on the fork, and verify all organizational invariants against the hypothetical post-action state. Catches violations BEFORE they occur, enabling preventive rather than reactive enforcement.

name: Dynamic Context Provenance Graph (DCPG) cross-session taint persistence
description: An offline provenance backbone that records how source content enters the agent context, flows through tool calls and memory operations, persists lineage across storage/session boundaries (serializing taint labels on store_in_memory/save_state and rehydrating on load_state/retrieve), and reconstructs the time-extended source-to-sink path. Bridges asynchronous provenance reuse so a source injected in one session is linked to a sink in a later session.

name: Sink-driven counterfactual causal analysis for implicit control influence
description: Detects implicit control influence (tainted source determines which/whether a sink fires with no data in sink args) by replacing the recovered tainted source with a task-neutral placeholder and asking an LLM judge whether the agent would still invoke the same sink with the same arguments. A counterfactual NO establishes that the tainted source causally drove the sink decision. Triggered only when no explicit taint is found, keeping cost bounded.

name: Argument-level provenance-aware capability contract (PACT)
description: A runtime monitor that equips each tool with an argument-level contract assigning semantic roles (target/command/credential/content/selector/control) over a trust lattice TRUSTED>USER>TOOL_OUTPUT>EXTERNAL, tracks value provenance across replanning steps, and before each invocation checks every argument against its role-specific minimum-trust requirement and forbidden-origin set. Permits external data in content roles while blocking it from binding authority-bearing arguments. Precision levels L0-L3 allow conservative coarse contracts that safely refine as argument semantics are specified; L3 supports scoped trusted discharge.

name: Trajectory-state final-action risk scoring (VISTA-Guard)
description: Backbone-agnostic defense for cognitive poisoning that abstracts an agent's exploratory tool interaction into structured environment-state variables (trigger-phase/probe/mismatch/identifier-drift/warning counts plus an auxiliary state_risk) and the proposed final action's executable parameter evidence, then scores whether the final tool-and-parameter bundle is compatible with the inferred trajectory state. Reasons about how trust formed across the trajectory rather than inspecting prompt text or single responses; evaluated under the asymmetric GuardedJoint metric that penalizes accepted-malicious over rejected-normal.

name: Delegated authorization constrained to semantic task-to-scope matching
description: Limit the privileges an agent can exercise to those whose scope semantically matches the authorized task, rather than granting the union of all tool privileges for the whole session. Combined with fine-grained per-task privilege scoping and plan validation, constrains the blast radius of privilege misuse when an agent is hijacked.

title: Attack-selection methodology (start/stop policy) for agentic control evaluations as a red-team elicitation tool
summary: Introduces a NEW red-team evaluation methodology that decomposes an agentic attacker's decision into two prompted scorer policies: a task-level START policy (scores each main-task/side-task pair 1-9 for how favorable an undetected side-task attack looks; attacks only when score>T*) and a per-turn STOP policy (scores in-progress conversation 1-9 for catch risk; aborts when score>T*). Both are implemented as prompted scorers (mimo-v2.5-pro, gpt-oss-120b) with thresholds tuned by 10-fold cross-validation, requiring NO model weight changes. Key result on two agentic control settings (BashArena: 637 tasks, 4 side tasks; LinuxArena: 1,667 main + 185 side tasks across 20 envs): at a 1% audit budget the start policy reduces empirical safety by -20pp on BOTH environments; the stop policy reduces it by -20pp (BashArena) and -28pp (LinuxArena, 0.36->0.09, Newcombe 95% CI [-37,-8]pp). Mechanism: selection changes WHICH trajectories get attacked (filters toward high-success, low-detection cases) rather than making attacks more capable. Authors frame this as an upper bound on prompted attack selection and call for system cards / safety cases to elicit attack selection.
notes: Genuine 2026 method shift: selective/strategic timing of attacks (vs i.i.d. fixed-rate attacker assumed by Greenblatt 2024 / Bhatt 2025 control framework). Companion to single-step Schaeffer et al. 2026 (BigCodeBench backdooring). Small-sample caveat at strict budgets: detecting <~25pp drops needs ~order-of-magnitude more trajectories (CIs narrow as 1/sqrt(qN)). Stop policy applied post-hoc (no feedback into agent actions) -> optimistic upper bound. Links to [[teaming-automated-attack-selection]].

title: Compute-aware (FLOP-based) red-team evaluation: risk-compute curves and C@tau / AE metrics
summary: Introduces a NEW red-team evaluation paradigm that re-parameterizes jailbreak benchmark results by cumulative FLOPs (computational pressure) instead of fixed query budget, importing the classical-security 'work factor' (Kerckhoffs) into LLM safety. Defines risk-compute curves (risk R vs cumulative FLOPs) and two scalar summary metrics: C@tau = avg cumulative TFLOPs to first reach tau% risk (tau=0.5 used), and AE (average efficiency) = normalized expected risk per FLOP (CAURC/Cmax). Per-step FLOP cost is modeled for each attack family (JailBroken template, PAIR iterative-refinement with Qwen2.5-7B attacker, GCG white-box suffix at 128+beta candidates). Five empirical findings with verbatim numbers: (1) alignment is NON-MONOTONIC -- Tulu3-SFT is most robust, DPO/RLVR erode it (GCG C@0.5 collapses 59.3->521.2 TFLOPs SFT->DPO; JailBroken ASR climbs to 0.90 at RLVR, +23% over DPO); (2) model scaling raises GCG cost 20x (0.5B->7B Qwen2.5) but JailBroken cost only 2.8x and ASR@10 barely drops 0.99->0.94 -- 7B remains 18x more exploitable per-TFLOP under JailBroken than GCG; (3) GCG suffixes optimized on Qwen2.5-0.5B surrogate transfer to closed Qwen3-8B (ASR@10=0.15) at fraction of cost; (4) compute-to-breach varies ~5x across harm categories; (5) Qwen3-4B-SafeRL can BACKFIRE -- strictly higher per-FLOP exploitability than base under GCG, and in cybercrime/illegal/misinformation categories. Cross-benchmark consistency Spearman rho>=0.91 (HarmBench vs JailbreakBench).
notes: Genuine 2026 method shift: judge-calibration framing + cost-accounting that exposes that ASR-at-fixed-budget systematically OVERSTATES robustness (echoes Nasr 2025: 12 defenses bypassed >90% ASR despite near-zero original reports). Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct used as the LLM-as-a-judge safety scorer at every attack step (judge-ensemble dimension). FLOP = 2NL forward approximation. Open-source framework 'r-three/risk-under-pressure'. Links to [[teaming-llm-as-a-judge]], [[teaming-automated-compute-aware-eval]].

name: Surrogate-to-target GCG transfer under compute budget

title: Spec-driven multi-agent security task synthesis with trajectory-aware execution evaluation (SeClaw)
summary: Introduces a NEW automated red-team task-GENERATION method: Spec-Driven Security Task Synthesis, a multi-agent collaborative pipeline (human experts + Claude Code) that builds executable agent security tasks from structured risk specifications rather than fixed human-curated instances, enabling scalable adaptation to emerging risks. Pipeline has three stages with quality gates: (1) task prototype synthesis (spec = risk type, task goal, risk source, safety constraints), (2) multi-agent task instantiation (workspace, MCP tools, mock_service, local_files, init.sh, task.yaml), (3) trajectory-based validation & iterative refinement (two-round: reference-solution round must pass an evaluator, then a normal round must be discriminative across models or fail as ineffective). Risk taxonomy organizes agent risks into four sources -- Resource, Task, Environment, Intrinsic -- mapping to consequences (data leakage, goal replacement, system instability, financial loss, privilege escalation, legal/compliance). Critically, SeClaw evaluates the EXECUTION PROCESS (tool calls, file ops, MCP calls, observations) not just final outputs, via a structured trajectory tau_i=(c_i, l_t, y_i, omega_i). Risk scoring uses coverage C=So/O, attack-success P=Sn/N, combined F_attack = 2CP/(C+P) (harmonic mean, F1-style risk-oriented score). Docker sandbox with FS/network/resource/permission isolation, one-instance-per-environment.
notes: Genuine 2026 method shift: spec-driven AUTOMATED generation of agent security eval tasks (vs static human-curated benchmarks), plus trajectory-aware (process-level) scoring. Self-described 'preliminary work / in progress'; evaluated on GPT-4o/Claude/Gemini/Qwen but quantitative model results not yet released -> evidence_grade B. ToolHub/MCP-based environment reconstruction is the MCP-security teaming bridge -- SHARE with agentic-se-risk-analyst. F_attack harmonic-mean metric is the method<->metric link. Links to [[teaming-automated-task-synthesis]], [[teaming-frontier-detection-trajectory-aware]].

title: LLM-as-a-defender: agentic cross-SIEM detection-rule conversion (ARuleCon) automates blue-team control portability
summary: Presents an LLM-as-a-DEFENDER teaming method that automates a blue-team control-engineering task: converting SIEM detection rules across heterogeneous vendors (Splunk SPL <-> Microsoft KQL <-> IBM AQL <-> Google YARA-L <-> RSA ESA). ARuleCon is an agentic closed-loop (generation -> verification -> testing -> optimization): (1) a vendor-agnostic Intermediate Representation IR=<M,S> decomposes each rule into ordered steps s_i=<KEYWORD,PARAM,DESCRIPTION> over 13 predefined functional keywords (FILTER, EXTRACT, AGGREGATE, OUTPUT, TRANSFORM, RENAME, LOOKUP, BUCKET, JOIN, FILL, APPEND, SORT, DEDUP, DEBUG); (2) an Agentic-RAG reflection agent iteratively queries official vendor docs (Chroma-indexed, text-embedding-ada-002, top-5) refining search until acceptance, fixing field/operator mismatches; (3) a Python-based consistency check compiles both IRs into executable functions, runs them over synthetic benign+attack logs, and feeds mismatches Delta=Os triangle Ot back as repair signals. On 1,492 conversion pairs across 5 SIEMs with GPT-5/DeepSeek-V3/LLaMA-3-405B: +9.1% CodeBLEU, +10.3% embedding similarity, +11.6% logic-slot consistency over baseline for GPT; execution success >90% (near-perfect for Splunk/Chronicle, 96-97% for IBM QRadar/RSA). Beats code-execution agents OpenHands/SWE-Agent. Failure modes: stateful-vs-stateless QRadar correlation flattening; temporal/aggregation mismatches in Sentinel/Chronicle.
notes: LLM-as-a-defender control-automation finding -- SHARE with risk-safety-analyst as a candidate control (detection-rule portability / SOC workload reduction). Sector: cybersecurity/SOC. First framework for agentic cross-SIEM rule conversion; complements rather than attacks. Efficiency cost: ~10x compute vs baseline (justified for high-stakes security translation per authors). Cohen's kappa>0.885 LLM-judge vs human. Links to [[teaming-llm-as-a-defender]].

name: Agentic cross-SIEM detection-rule conversion (ARuleCon-style)
description: An agentic LLM control that ports existing SIEM detection rules across vendor query languages via a vendor-agnostic IR, RAG-grounded refinement against vendor docs, and Python-execution-based functional-equivalence verification. Preserves blue-team detection coverage during platform migration/multi-vendor operation, reducing manual SOC rework and the risk of missed detections from naive rule translation.

title: Agent-Human Interaction (AHI) security reframe: human-in-the-loop as the dominant deployed teaming method, with a quantified industry-academia mismatch
summary: SoK reframing LLM-agent security defense as an Agent-Human Interaction (AHI) problem and quantifying a stark industry<->academia mismatch in human-AI teaming mechanisms. Analyzes 59 papers + 21 production agent systems + 26 security plugins (Apr 2026), deriving five AHI defense categories via axial coding. Adoption table (Papers/Systems/Rate): Scope & Boundary Config 4/16/76%, Runtime Approval 5/15/71%, Policy Specification 13/14/67%, Trust & Data Labeling 8/0/0%, Intent Anchoring 5/0/0%. Core finding: the academia-favored fully-automated categories (intent anchoring, trust labeling -- which delegate intent judgment to an LLM-as-a-judge) have ZERO production deployment, while the three human-centric mechanisms back every one of 21 deployed systems (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Manus). Argues human participation is irreplaceable (5 reasons: imprecise prompts, irreducible ambiguity -- interactive clarification improves task success up to 74%, circular dependency of LLM-judge being itself attackable via prompt injection, direct expression > inference, 21/21 industry convergence). But ALL deployed mechanisms hit a cognitive-burden vs security-guarantee Pareto trade-off (approval fatigue: SSL-warning-style 90%+ click-through; scope creep: Replit prod-DB deletion July 2025; AgentSpec NL policy generation only 70.96% recall; AutoPermissions LLM approval prediction 85.1%). Proposes 3 research directions: fatigue-resistant (risk-adaptive RTBAS, bidirectional scope), usable policy/trust, LLM-AUGMENTED (assistive not decisional) intent alignment.
notes: Genuine 2026 method shift: establishes HUMAN-AI teaming (not pure automation) as the empirically dominant agent-security paradigm and names AHI security a first-class subfield. The circular-dependency reason (LLM-judge guarding LLM is itself attackable) is the key red-team insight -- SHARE with agentic-se-risk-analyst (prompt-injection on LLM-as-judge defenders). 'future.llm-augmented-intent' marked emerging (not future) per conservative rule -- it is a proposed research agenda but AutoPermissions/LLM-drafted-policy precursors already exist ^[ambiguous]. Links to [[teaming-human-ai-runtime-approval]], [[teaming-llm-as-a-judge]].

title: Agentic LLM-as-a-defender for hardware IP obfuscation -- a defensive teaming pipeline that SAT attacks still fully break
summary: Evaluates an agentic LLM-as-a-DEFENDER pipeline for the hardware-security sector: automated netlist logic-obfuscation (key-controlled locking) to protect IC IP against reverse engineering/piracy/overbuilding. The agentic workflow separates LLM reasoning from deterministic validation across stages: retrieval-grounded planning (topology-aware ranking of lock targets by depth/fanout/output-cone), LLM synthesis of a structured lock-plan (targets, lock style, helper signals, key-bit groups), deterministic renderer/compiler to legal .bench (ABC/Yosys), functional verification (parse validity, correct-key match, wrong-key corruption), PySAT distinguishing-input-pattern (DIP) attack evaluation, and an LLM refinement agent closing the loop. Lock styles: xor_xnor, perturb_restore, mux_lock, pairwise_subgraph, hybrid. Evaluated on 8 ISCAS-85 circuits x {8,16,32-bit keys} x {GPT-5, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B} = 72 runs. KEY DEFENSIVE LIMITATION FINDING: all models produce valid correct-key netlists with measurable wrong-key corruption (0.01-0.23; c432 highest, c5315 lowest) BUT the SAT/DIP attack RECOVERS THE CORRECT KEY IN ALL CASES -- larger keys raise DIP attack effort (4->15 mean DIPs as 8->32 bit) but never prevent recovery. Aggregates: GPT-5 corr 0.050 / 9.6 DIPs / 209s; LLaMA 0.051 / 8.0 / 66s; Qwen 0.045 / 9.1 / 114s.
notes: Sector-specific (hardware/IC supply-chain) LLM-as-a-defender teaming finding -- I own the method axis; SHARE the negative result (agentic obfuscation still SAT-breakable) with risk-safety-analyst as a residual-risk note. Honest negative finding: current LLM-generated lock templates increase attack COST but provide no real resistance; also notes side-channel (power leakage) vulnerability orthogonal to key recovery. SAT-based DIP attack here is the red-team/attack side of an otherwise defensive pipeline. Links to [[teaming-llm-as-a-defender]].

title: Per-release privacy defenses fail to bound cumulative, indirect inference leakage across an agent trajectory
summary: OCELOT formalizes three properties that defeat deployed agent-privacy defenses: (P1) leakage is cumulative — individually innocuous releases combine across honest-but-curious or colluding sinks to reconstruct a secret no single message names; (P2) leakage is bidirectional — ingested observations can inject instructions that subvert the reasoning model into leaking more on later turns; (P3) leakage is task-dependent — the same field is necessary for one sink and gratuitous for another. On long-horizon stress (up to 50 steps) per-release contextual-integrity filters (FlexGuard, PrivacyChecker) and monitors keep approving fresh disclosures, growing ~linearly and crossing a B*=4.0-bit budget near steps 18-24, while OCELOT's cumulative leakage saturates below 1.0 bit. Against a colluding adversary across all channels, OCELOT top-1 secret recovery is 4.2% vs 27.3-64.8% for non-CaMeL baselines; collusion rises from 1.2% at one sink to 11.9% at eight sinks for OCELOT vs baselines reaching 33.6-71.5%. The mechanism gives a two-layer guarantee: deductive budget non-exceedance (zero exceedances over 22,585 trajectory-instances) by ledger arithmetic independent of any LLM, plus an empirical calibration-relative semantic-privacy claim.
notes: Verbatim: OCELOT recovery 4.2% under collusion vs 27.3-64.8% baselines; injection success 3.8% vs 8.1-67.4%; defender-jailbreak escape rate delta=1.7%; 18% wall-clock overhead; B*=4.0 bits. Two-layer guarantee (deductive budget + empirical semantic privacy) is the novel contribution. Witness-Verified Declassification = untrusted defender LLM + deterministic verifier.

title: Witness-Verified Declassification: an honest-but-jailbreakable defender under a deterministic verifier as a privacy control pattern
summary: OCELOT's control separates semantic judgment (needs an LLM) from authorization (must not depend on an LLM). An untrusted, locally fine-tuned defender labels each candidate release with structured atoms/operators and a proposal; a deterministic trusted verifier re-checks labels against signed rubrics, computes a certified min-entropy cost via calibrated adversarial-inference upper-confidence bounds (audited with a bounded-treewidth credal circuit), and authorizes the least-disclosing variant (operators: IDENTITY<GENERALIZE<SUBSTITUTE<REDACT<DROP) under a sink-trust-weighted budget recorded on a Merkle-chained ledger. Because the verifier costs any unlabeled or mislabeled atom at worst-case risk, a jailbroken defender yields a conservative fallback, never silent leakage. The defender is trained via SFT on 82,400 rubric-application examples (37% omission, 21% injection, 19% distribution-shift) plus GRPO with verifier-conformance reward. Inbound tool output is rendered in a quoted-data wrapper that strips authority semantics, countering bidirectional injection structurally rather than by detection.
notes: Control = runtime privacy mediator with deductive budget guarantee. Removing rubric coverage raises escape rate delta from 1.7%->11.3%; removing conservative default -> 1 raw field leaked (2.18 bits, injection 12.7%) = empirical Layer-1b backstop. Defender-independence: budget non-exceedance holds even with rule-based declassifier (OCELOT-).

hazard: Individually-innocuous PII releases by an LLM agent accumulate across turns and across colluding/honest-but-curious sinks to reconstruct a protected secret that no single release names
hazardous_situation: A multi-step agent (booking, medical-intake, financial-onboarding) discloses task-necessary fields to multiple external sinks; per-release contextual-integrity filters approve each disclosure in isolation, but the union of releases lets an adversary infer the user's secret with high posterior probability over a long-horizon trajectory
controls: Merkle-chained cumulative leakage ledger (sink-trust-weighted budget non-exceedance)
quoted-data wrapper stripping authority from inbound observations
calibrated per-operator min-entropy cost with credal-circuit audit
residual_risk: Low-to-moderate under OCELOT: deductive budget non-exceedance is exact (0 exceedances / 22,585 instances) so the cumulative bit-budget cannot be exceeded; but the semantic-privacy claim is empirical and calibration-relative — residual escape rate delta=1.7% when a jailbroken defender mislabels an atom outside the verifier's field set, and leave-one-category-out transfer leaks up to 0.74 bits on inference-heavy domains (still below all baselines). Residual depends on calibration of C(op,f) upper-bounding true adversarial inference.

name: Witness-Verified Declassification (untrusted defender + deterministic verifier + leakage budget ledger)
description: A runtime privacy mediator inside the agent harness that intercepts every release crossing the trust boundary. An untrusted, locally fine-tuned defender LLM emits structured evidence (labeled atoms, declassification operators, hashed proposal); a deterministic trusted verifier re-checks the labels against signed rubrics, charges a certified min-entropy cost from calibrated upper-confidence bounds, and authorizes only the least-disclosing variant under a sink-trust-weighted per-trajectory budget recorded on a tamper-evident Merkle/Ed25519 ledger. Conservative defaults cost any unlabeled/mislabeled atom at worst-case risk so a jailbroken or omitting defender yields fallback (redact/drop/escalate-to-user), never silent leakage. Inbound observations are rendered in an authority-stripping quoted-data wrapper to block injection structurally.

title: Foundation-model robots are functionally capable yet physically unsafe due to missing systematic hazard grounding, with high false-negative rates on safety-critical edge cases
summary: Physical-AI robots adapt to novel tasks via in-context learning/fine-tuning but, being trained for task performance, lack systematic grounding in hazard awareness — producing actions that are functionally correct yet physically unsafe. The paper formalizes a hazard h:S->{0,1} and safety rule r:S->{0,1} over system states and shows the scenario space is the Cartesian product of objects x robot actions x environmental conditions x human behaviors, which explodes combinatorially so exhaustive enumeration of safety-critical edge cases is infeasible. A controlled Webots proof-of-concept (table-edge can-placement safe/unsafe classifier, 5 videos, 258 sampled frames) achieved precision 0.9913 but recall only 0.6869 (F1 0.8115, accuracy 0.8936), with a Type II error rate of 0.3131 — i.e. ~31% of hazardous configurations are misclassified as safe, concentrated near the safe/unsafe decision boundary. The cited literature notes Vision-Language-Action models offer safety opportunities but introduce amplified risks from scarce real-world contact data; LongSafety found most LLMs achieve <55% safety rates in long-context robot tasks.
notes: Verbatim: precision 0.9913, recall 0.6869, Type II error 0.3131, F1 0.8115, accuracy 0.8936. High false-negative rate on boundary hazard cases is the safety-load-bearing result. Paper is research-in-progress (problem formulation + PoC), not a fully evaluated system.

title: Red-Team/Blue-Team adversarial gamification as a control for discovering long-tail physical-safety edge cases
summary: The paper reframes safety-scenario discovery (not scenario learning) as the bottleneck and proposes a two-player adversarial game over a digital twin of the target home plus an object-vulnerability registry. A Red Team agent (human or AI with a reward maximizing hazard probability) constructs sequences of robot actions, object placements, and human movements that cause a hazard (cup shattering, spill, collision) within the allowed physics; a Blue Team agent (safety policy) refines rules after each round (e.g. 'prohibit gripper approach vectors from above when handling the blue vase'). Every attempted scenario, successful or not, is logged into a boundary-focused synthetic dataset for fine-tuning / in-context learning, yielding a learned safety envelope plus an auditable trail of why each rule was added. The approach supports lifelong re-running when the environment changes and crowdsourced human adversaries. This positions adversarial red-teaming as a safety-by-design data-generation control for embodied agents, addressing the false-negative gap documented in the PoC.
notes: Framework is proposed but not yet evaluated end-to-end (no gamification results reported beyond the simpler classifier PoC). Evidence_grade B: the control's effectiveness claim is conceptual. Hazard-informed 5-stage pipeline: asset declaration->exposure modes->hazard scenario->synthetic data->safety envelope learning.

hazard: A foundation-model-controlled home/service robot fails to recognize a physically hazardous state (e.g. object near a low-friction table edge, missed human detection from sensor occlusion) because its task-trained perception lacks systematic hazard grounding and under-covers long-tail boundary cases
hazardous_situation: A general-purpose robot deployed into an unseen, personalized domestic environment acts on context-agnostic universal safety rules; a rare combination (misestimated edge position + low-friction surface + a human bumping the table) produces a falling/collision hazard that the safety classifier misses (~31% false-negative rate near the decision boundary)
controls: hazard-informed 5-stage engineering pipeline (asset declaration->exposure modes->hazard scenario->synthetic data->safety-envelope learning)
environment-specific safety grounding (digital twin + object-vulnerability registry)
residual_risk: Moderate: the PoC classifier still misses ~31% of unsafe configurations (recall 0.6869), concentrated near the safe/unsafe boundary; the proposed Red/Blue gamification framework that targets these boundary cases is conceptual and not yet validated end-to-end, so residual physical-injury risk in open-ended environments remains substantial pending real-world deployment evaluation. ^[ambiguous] effectiveness of gamification at reducing false negatives is asserted, not measured.

name: Red-Team/Blue-Team adversarial gamification for embodied safety-scenario generation
description: A two-player adversarial game over a high-fidelity physics simulator/digital twin of the deployment environment plus a registry of objects and their declared vulnerabilities. A Red Team agent (human or reward-driven AI) iteratively constructs action/object/human-movement sequences that produce a physical hazard within allowed physics; a Blue Team agent refines the robot's safety policy after each round to prevent the discovered hazard. All attempts are logged into a boundary-focused synthetic dataset used to fine-tune perception, train anomaly detectors, and learn a safety envelope, with an auditable trail linking each safety rule to the scenario that necessitated it. Re-runnable for lifelong safety learning when the environment or robot capabilities change.

title: High medical-exam accuracy does not guarantee deployment safety; medical LLMs need auditable safety/ethics alignment and adversarial-misuse resilience
summary: SafeMed-R1 (built on Qwen3-32B, SFT on 320,710 QA-CoT items + GRPO with a 10,000-prompt red-team dataset) argues that exam-style accuracy is a prerequisite but insufficient for clinical governance, identifying three gaps: (1) limited governance-grade supervision for reasoning-style outputs, (2) ethics/safety rarely treated as first-class objectives, (3) under-studied system-level robustness under adversarial misuse. It reaches 79.6% macro-average accuracy (vs base Qwen3-32B 77.7%, its SFT variant 78.3%, strongest external Baichuan-M2-32B 77.6%), scores 81.3 on MedSafety and 80.7 on MedEthics, and under MedSafetyBench (MSB) adversarial audit shows the lowest aggregated risk, reducing unsafe behavior ~3-5% vs baseline. The red-team set targets unauthorized diagnostic/prescribing requests, guideline-violating treatments, misleading harmful instructions, and role-induction attacks. A five-retry screening (re-answer with DeepSeek-R1) escalated the 6.4% of items failing all five attempts to expert adjudication. The work warns benign exam-style testing underestimates real-world risk, and that prompt-injection/jailbreak vulnerabilities persist in medical multimodal settings.
notes: Verbatim: 79.6% macro accuracy, MedSafety 81.3, MedEthics 80.7, ~3-5% unsafe-output reduction vs baseline, 6.4% items failed all 5 retries. Red-team strategies: role play, boundary probing, purpose inversion, scene construction. Normative-ethics subdomains (end-of-life, mental health, TCM, public-health emergencies) lag operational-safety subdomains and are flagged for targeted red-teaming.

title: Clinical Trust Signals: clinician-audited supervision provenance as an auditable governance control for medical-LLM safety
summary: SafeMed-R1's Clinical Trust Signals (CTS) is a supervision-provenance scheme (distinct from inference-time citation grounding) linking each QA-CoT reasoning item to five-dimensional clinician rubric scores, edit histories, and adjudication decisions, enabling clinicians/governance teams to verify adherence to explicit safety/ethics checks, localize failures to actionable risk categories for remediation, and quantify worst-case unsafe behavior. From 362,130 candidate QA-CoT pairs, multi-stage review by 160 physicians across 14 specialties over 2 months retained 311,088 items (81% no edits, 16% revised, 3% removed as irreparable; all retained items approved by >=2 licensed clinicians). Risk decomposition across MedSafety/MedEthics subdomains showed Reasoning Structure (Score 1: 94.2%) and Information Completeness (Score 1: 94.6%; Score 0: 5.4%) as the governable bottlenecks. In a paired study on 30 medication-safety vignettes, SafeMed-R1 matched PGY1/PGY2 residents on medical correctness (4.73+/-0.83 vs 4.53+/-0.68, p=0.23) but scored higher on medication-safety adequacy, guideline consistency, and clinical usefulness (median 5.0 vs 4.0; r~0.73; all p<0.001).
notes: Verbatim: 362,130->311,088 retained (81%/16%/3%); 160 physicians/14 specialties/2 months; >=2 clinician approval; paired correctness 4.73 vs 4.53 p=0.23, safety/guideline/usefulness median 5.0 vs 4.0 r~0.73 p<0.001. CTS = supervision-level provenance, NOT inference-time evidence attribution (explicitly orthogonal). Limitation: text-only, no multimodal/cross-modal safety failure modes evaluated; reconstructed de-identified vignettes not prospective deployment.

hazard: A medical LLM with high exam-style accuracy produces unsafe, ethically-misaligned, or guideline-violating clinical outputs under adversarial misuse or value-sensitive contexts (informed consent, refusal, vulnerable populations) that benign benchmark testing fails to surface
hazardous_situation: A clinician-facing or patient-facing medical assistant is targeted by role-induction, boundary-probing, purpose-inversion, or jailbreak prompts (unauthorized diagnosis/prescribing, guideline-violating treatment), or is queried in a normative-ethics-heavy scenario (end-of-life, mental health, public-health emergency) where the model's safety performance is weakest
controls: safety/ethics-as-first-class GRPO alignment with reward over medical-ethics criteria
MedSafetyBench adversarial stress testing + multi-judge ensemble scoring
five-retry consistency screening with expert escalation of failures
subdomain risk-decomposition to prioritize targeted red-teaming of weak normative-ethics categories
residual_risk: Moderate: SafeMed-R1 reduces unsafe behavior only ~3-5% relative to baseline and shows lowest aggregated risk among evaluated systems, but residual unsafe outputs persist, normative-ethics subdomains (end-of-life, mental health, TCM) remain weaker and explicitly flagged for further red-teaming, and the evaluation is text-only — multimodal/cross-modal safety failure modes are unquantified ^[ambiguous]. No prospective in-workflow deployment data, so real-world over-reliance and error-interception rates are unmeasured.

name: Clinical Trust Signals (CTS) — clinician-audited supervision provenance for medical-LLM governance
description: A traceable supervision-provenance pipeline that links each medical QA chain-of-thought training/evaluation item to structured clinician rubric scores (five dimensions), edit histories, and panel-adjudication decisions, producing an auditable trail that lets clinicians and governance teams verify adherence to explicit safety/ethics checks, localize failures to actionable risk categories for remediation, and quantify worst-case unsafe behavior. Operationalized via multi-stage review (here 160 physicians across 14 specialties), >=2-clinician approval per retained item, LLM-based adversarial re-answering with consistency screening, and subdomain risk decomposition (MedSafety/MedEthics) that bridges to targeted red-teaming of weak categories. Distinct from and complementary to inference-time citation grounding.

title: Reasoning scaffolds calibrate but cannot manufacture missing evidence: the proprietary evidence substrate sets the decision-quality ceiling for AI Scientist agents
summary: A controlled three-arm ablation (A: plain LLM+web; B: +skills/public tools/verifier/objectivity-charter/red-team; C: +proprietary database) over an identical production drug-asset valuation agent on Claude Code with Opus 4.8 MAX, on a 13-asset benchmark stratified by five decision archetypes (28-30 scored cells/condition), shows the non-proprietary tool/skills layer improves how evidence is used but not the factual ceiling. B raises tier-in-range accuracy 0.80->0.89 and objectivity 3.16->3.30 and corrects a plain-agent failure mode (indiscriminate pessimism — A returns no_go on every validated-mechanism white-space S2 asset, tier-in-range 0.0). But under generous capability-superset accounting A and B recover only 0.25 and 0.38 of the curated gold competitive record while C recovers 0.96; on the curated long-tail subset C reaches 0.93 vs 0.26/0.30. Raw blind-panel decision-quality is similar for A and B (7.01 vs 6.96), but completeness-aware informed decision-quality (DQ x gold-coverage) is 7.43 for C vs 1.76/2.57 for A/B — and even a hypothetical perfect non-proprietary report (DQ=10) is capped at 3.83 by B's 0.38 coverage, below C's observed score. False-GO rate is 0.0 for all arms; the discriminating error is under-valuation, not over-valuation.
notes: Verbatim: R_gold A/B/C = 0.25/0.38/0.96; long-tail recall 0.26/0.30/0.93; informed-DQ 1.76/2.57/7.43; tier-in-range 0.80/0.89/0.89; objectivity 3.16/3.30/3.60; B's perfect-report informed-DQ ceiling 3.83; false-GO 0.0 all arms. Gold-set circularity caveat (keys seeded from same proprietary family) noted by authors. Capability-superset accounting is generous to B/C yet B still only 0.38.

title: Attributing AI Scientist capability to model/prompt/scaffold without an evidence-substrate ablation produces a misleading safety/validity case in knowledge-intensive domains
summary: The paper shows practitioners observe the combined system and attribute quality to 'the model', 'the prompt', or 'the data' without ablation, conflating two distinct enhancements (reasoning skills + public tools vs proprietary curated data). This creates an evaluation-validity hazard: a methodologically sound, verdict-first, evidence-tiered report can be scientifically under-informed if written over the wrong evidence base — A and B have near-identical raw verdict-soundness (7.01 vs 6.96) yet operate over only ~25-38% of the competitive field, so a sound verdict over an incomplete substrate is silently low-quality. The plain agent's failure is indiscriminate pessimism (systematically under-valuing validated-mechanism white-space opportunities), not recklessness; objectivity charters and red-team passes that only lower recommendations cannot surface missing long-tail evidence. The diagnostic introduces completeness-aware decision utility to separate reasoning discipline from evidence substrate, and warns that for knowledge-intensive AI Scientist systems the decisive capability comes from access to curated/long-tail evidence rather than another reasoning prompt — with implications for how autonomous scientific agents should be benchmarked and trusted.
notes: Threats-to-validity acknowledged: no clean payoff ground truth, judge bias (hard-blind 3-judge panel, inter-judge std ~0.5), gold-set circularity, capability-superset generosity, small/uneven strata. The framing risk (evidence-substrate confound in AI-Scientist eval) is the novel safety-relevant signal; classify under safety.capability-risk + evaluation validity.

hazard: An autonomous AI Scientist agent produces a methodologically sound but scientifically under-informed high-stakes recommendation because its evidence substrate (proprietary/curated/long-tail record) covers only a fraction of the relevant field, and the gap is invisible to verdict-soundness and objectivity evaluation
hazardous_situation: A knowledge-intensive AI Scientist agent (e.g. drug-asset go/no-go valuation, ~$2.6B-per-approval decisions) reasons over web + public APIs only; it issues a calibrated, objective, red-teamed verdict over ~25-38% of the competitive/long-tail evidence, and downstream decision-makers trust the recommendation because raw verdict-soundness looks high while completeness is unmeasured
controls: stratified-by-archetype benchmarking that predicts factual-vs-calibration failure per stratum
capability-superset accounting + curated gold/long-tail coverage metrics (R_gold, long-tail recall)
layered architecture: public tools/skills for calibration + proprietary corpus for informed verdicts
hard-blind multi-judge panel with provenance-scrubbed reports
residual_risk: Moderate: completeness-aware informed decision-quality exposes the gap (C 7.43 vs A/B 1.76/2.57) but the evaluation itself rests on a curated proprietary gold set seeded from the same family available to arm C (gold-set circularity ^[ambiguous]), so it favors the data-enabled arm and is not an independent clinical-payoff ground truth; no clean real-world outcome anchor exists (asset value settles over years). The factual-coverage ceiling is structural — reasoning scaffolds cannot close it — so residual under-informed-decision risk persists wherever long-tail/proprietary evidence is unavailable.

name: Completeness-aware decision-utility evaluation for AI Scientist agents
description: An evaluation methodology that separates reasoning discipline (tier calibration, objectivity, blind-panel verdict-soundness) from the evidence substrate (coverage of a curated competitive/long-tail record, R_gold, long-tail recall) and combines them into informed decision-quality = decision-quality x gold-coverage, so a sound verdict written over an incomplete evidence base scores low. Uses a benchmark stratified by decision archetype (each stratum chosen so its known structure predicts whether failure should be factual incompleteness, calibration error, or both), capability-superset accounting, and a hard-blind multi-judge panel scored on provenance-scrubbed reports. Surfaces the otherwise-invisible evidence-substrate ceiling and the indiscriminate-pessimism calibration failure of plain agents.

title: MoE routing is topic-driven, not safety-intent-driven: refusal is mediated inside expert representations, exposing a localized expert-level safety vulnerability
summary: Across three complementary routing probes on aligned open-weight MoE LLMs the paper shows routers are organized around semantic topic, not the refusal/compliance distinction or unsafe intent: (1) teacher-forced refusal vs compliant continuations for the same harmful prompt produce near-identical top-8 expert overlap (e.g. 7.18-7.92) and small router-logit JS divergence (0.0054-0.0434); (2) adding a refusal-inducing prefix under a fixed topic shifts routing little (JSD 0.0098-0.0346) while changing topic under the same refusal style shifts it much more (JSD 0.3379); (3) matched harmful/benign prompt pairs that preserve topic but flip intent give JSD 0.1006 vs 0.2362/0.2282 for random cross-topic pairs. Therefore safety enforcement resides in the representations of topic-specialized experts that are naturally activated, not in distinct safety-routed experts — implying router-steering attacks misdirect tokens to mismatched experts and degrade utility, whereas expert-representation-level edits can flip safety while preserving routing.
notes: Verbatim JSD: teacher-forced refusal-vs-compliant 0.0054-0.0434; refusal-prefix fixed-topic 0.0098-0.0346 vs topic-change 0.3379; matched intent-flip 0.1006 vs random cross-topic 0.2282-0.2362. Five MoE backbones: OLMoE-1B-7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, Phi-3.5-MoE-instruct, GPT-oss-20b. Novel locus: safety lives in expert params, not routing path.

title: RASET: router-agnostic safety-critical expert tuning reprograms a tiny fraction of MoE parameters to bypass alignment while preserving routing and utility
summary: RASET is a MoE red-teaming framework that identifies safety-critical experts via a contrastive routing-sensitivity score S_{l,i}=A(l,i;D_harm)-lambda*A(l,i;D_norm) (subtracting benign activation to isolate experts disproportionately recruited by harmful queries), then applies parameter-efficient tuning only to the top-K selected experts while freezing the router, shared components, and all non-selected experts. A dual loss promotes affirmative continuations / suppresses refusal prefixes (max-margin penalty) while an L2 + benign-NLL preservation loss keeps utility. Across five MoE backbones RASET reaches the highest red-teaming yield at every strictness level: 78.6% ASR_raw, 74.0% ASR_valid, 50.5% ASR_hq (outperforming the strongest GCG baseline by 37.6 points on average) while updating only 0.12-0.95% of parameters. Routing stays nearly intact (post-tuning JS divergence below 0.04, top-8 expert overlap deviation below 8%; harmful-query JSD 0.0811, overlap 5.66) and utility degrades modestly (TruthfulQA 68.9->63.4, MMLU 69.9->62.4, drops 5.4 / 7.5 points). This demonstrates MoE safety alignment can be compromised through small expert-level changes even when routing is preserved.
notes: Verbatim: ASR_raw 78.6%, ASR_valid 74.0%, ASR_hq 50.5%, +37.6pt over GCG; params updated 0.12-0.95%; utility drop TruthfulQA 5.4pt / MMLU 7.5pt; routing JSD<0.04, overlap deviation<8%. Per-model ASR_hq: DeepSeek 61.5, Qwen3 71.5, OLMoE 50.5, GPT-oss 39.5, Phi 29.5. Attack requires white-box weight access. Maps to ATLAS T0018 (backdoor/model tampering).

hazard: An attacker with white-box access to an open-weight MoE LLM reprograms a tiny subset of safety-critical experts (0.12-0.95% of parameters) to flip alignment from refusal to compliance on harmful requests while leaving the router and topic-specialized expert routing path nearly unchanged
hazardous_situation: An open-weight MoE model is fine-tuned by a malicious actor using a contrastive routing-sensitivity criterion (RASET) to locate and reprogram safety-mediating experts; the resulting model passes routing-stability and benign-utility checks (utility drop <8 points) yet produces high-quality harmful outputs (50.5% ASR_hq), evading defenses that monitor router behavior or assume safety lives on a distinct routing path
controls: expert-level integrity monitoring of safety-critical experts (vs router-only monitoring)
weight-release governance / gated access for high-capability MoE models
