name: Reconnaissance
description: The adversary gathers information about the target AI system, its model, data, guardrails, and surrounding software to plan and tailor an attack.

name: Resource Development
description: The adversary establishes resources to support operations — poisoned datasets/knowledge bases, malicious packages, or implanted backdoors usable later in the attack lifecycle.

name: Initial Access
description: The adversary gains an initial foothold by getting malicious instructions or inputs into the AI system — via direct jailbreak prompts, indirect injection through tools/RAG, poisoned tool descriptions, or spoofed agent identities.

name: AI Model Access
description: The adversary obtains a level of access to the AI model — white-box gradients, query access, or physical/sensor access — sufficient to stage and optimize an attack against it.

name: Execution
description: The adversary runs adversary-controlled behavior on the AI system or its environment — coercing a tool-using agent to invoke tools, run code, or take actions on the attacker's behalf.

name: Persistence
description: The adversary maintains a foothold across retraining, fine-tuning, or restarts — e.g. a conditional backdoor that survives safety training and re-activates on its trigger.

name: Privilege Escalation
description: The adversary gains higher-level permissions within an agentic system — abusing confused-deputy tool wiring or spoofing a trusted agent identity to obtain capabilities it should not have.

name: Defense Evasion
description: The adversary avoids detection by guardrails, monitors, classifiers, screening, or human reviewers — including covert subversion of oversight, sandbagging on evaluations, collusion to pass review, and stealth that defeats filters over time.

name: Discovery
description: The adversary probes the deployed system to learn its internal state, tools, situational context, or guardrail boundaries — situational-awareness probing that informs whether and how to act covertly.

name: Collection
description: The adversary gathers sensitive data from the AI system — coaxing the model to disclose training data, system prompts, or retrieved private context that becomes the staging ground for exfiltration.

name: AI Attack Staging
description: The adversary leverages knowledge of and access to the model to craft, optimize, and stage the actual adversarial input — suffix optimization, iterative refinement, evolutionary/QD search, or perturbation crafting prior to delivery.

name: Command and Control
description: The adversary establishes a covert channel to control compromised agents — using indirect injection or spoofed inter-agent messages to direct ongoing agent behavior from untrusted content.

name: Exfiltration
description: The adversary extracts AI artifacts or sensitive information out of the target environment — model weights self-exfiltrated by an autonomous model, or private/training data drawn out through multi-turn leakage.

name: Impact
description: The adversary manipulates, degrades, or weaponizes the AI system to cause real-world harm — physical autonomous failure, biosecurity uplift, sabotaged code shipped to production, or harmful content/cyber uplift at scale.

title: GCG generates universal adversarial suffixes that transfer across aligned LLMs
summary: Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) uses greedy + gradient search to produce adversarial suffixes that make aligned LLMs emit harmful content, and the suffixes transfer from open-source (Llama-2, Vicuna) to proprietary models (ChatGPT, Bard, Claude). The AdvBench 520-behavior set became the foundational jailbreak benchmark reused by HarmBench/JailbreakBench.

title: PAIR jailbreaks black-box LLMs with semantic prompts in <20 queries via attacker-LLM refinement
summary: PAIR (Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement) uses an attacker LLM applying social-engineering tactics to iteratively craft and refine semantic jailbreaks against a target with black-box access only, often succeeding in fewer than twenty queries and transferring across GPT-3.5/4, Vicuna, and Gemini.

title: TAP jailbreaks GPT-4-class models >80% of the time with fewer queries via pruned tree search
summary: Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP) has an attacker LLM iteratively refine candidate prompts in a tree search, pruning unpromising branches before querying the target. It jailbreaks GPT-4-Turbo/GPT-4o for >80% of prompts with fewer queries than prior black-box methods and penetrates guardrails such as Llama Guard.

title: GPTFuzzer auto-mutates seed templates to reach >90% ASR across ChatGPT/Llama-2/Vicuna
summary: GPTFuzzer applies fuzzing to jailbreak template generation: starting from human seed templates, it mutates them via coverage-guided seed selection, semantic mutation operators, and a judgment model, exceeding manually crafted templates and reaching over 90% attack success even from suboptimal seeds.

title: Rainbow Teaming uses quality-diversity (MAP-Elites) search to mine >90% ASR diverse adversarial prompts
summary: Rainbow Teaming casts adversarial prompt generation as a quality-diversity problem over MAP-Elites, producing hundreds of diverse, transferable adversarial prompts against Llama 2/3 with attack success >90%. The synthetic prompts double as safety-tuning data that improves robustness without hurting helpfulness.

title: RainbowPlus pushes QD adversarial search to 81.1% ASR on HarmBench across 12 LLMs, ~9x faster
summary: RainbowPlus extends MAP-Elites with a multi-element archive and concurrent fitness evaluation, reaching an average 81.1% attack success rate on HarmBench across twelve LLMs while generating far more unique prompts (e.g., 10,418 vs 100) and running ~9x faster than prior QD baselines — a direct 2025 successor to Rainbow Teaming.

title: GFlowNet red-teaming defeats RL attacker mode-collapse, yielding diverse transferable attack prompts
summary: A GFlowNet-based automated red-teaming method generates diverse, effective attack prompts, overcoming the mode collapse that limits PPO/REINFORCE attackers even with diversity regularization. A GFlowNet fine-tuning + smoothing pipeline produces attacks that transfer across target models and harden safety tuning when reused as training data.

title: Promptbreeder's self-referential prompt evolution is the methodological ancestor of QD red-teaming
summary: Promptbreeder evolves both task-prompts and the mutation-prompts themselves across generations via an LLM. Though not safety-specific, its self-referential evolutionary prompt-optimization is the mechanism Rainbow Teaming's quality-diversity adversarial generation builds on.
notes: ^[inferred] jailbreak/prompt-attack mapping is by lineage to Rainbow Teaming, not a safety claim in the source itself.

title: StrongREJECT shows jailbreak effectiveness is widely overstated; many jailbreaks also degrade capability
summary: StrongREJECT provides forbidden prompts plus an automated evaluator scoring how much *useful* harmful information a response gives. It finds jailbreak developers substantially exaggerate effectiveness for lack of a standard benchmark, and that many jailbreaks bypassing safety fine-tuning also reduce the model's underlying capabilities.
notes: Methodological finding: measurement validity of ASR claims, not a new attack.

title: HarmBench standardizes ASR across 18 red-team methods x 33 target LLMs/defenses
summary: HarmBench is a standardized automated-red-teaming evaluation framework spanning standard, contextual, copyright, and multimodal harmful behaviors, using attack success rate as the primary metric. Its large-scale comparison of 18 attack methods against 33 targets/defenses, plus the R2D2 adversarial-training baseline, set a reproducibility floor for jailbreak measurement.

title: JailbreakBench maintains an evolving jailbreak-artifact repository and standardized attack/defense leaderboard
summary: JailbreakBench supplies an evolving repository of state-of-the-art jailbreak artifacts, the JBB-Behaviors dataset (100 misuse + 100 benign behaviors aligned to OpenAI policy), a standardized threat-model + LLM-judge evaluation, and a public attack/defense leaderboard, enabling stable cross-method comparison.

title: AgentDojo measures indirect prompt-injection hijacking of tool-using agents over untrusted data
summary: AgentDojo is a dynamic environment evaluating tool-calling agents over untrusted data, with 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases. It shows existing prompt-injection attacks break some — but not all — security properties of state-of-the-art agents, and that agents fail many tasks even without attacks, framing indirect injection as a live attacker/defender benchmark.
notes: Owns the attack technique (indirect injection); agent-risk lens owns the agent hijacking risk.

title: AgentHarm shows simple jailbreak templates transfer to multi-step tool-using agents
summary: AgentHarm benchmarks the harmfulness of text tool-calling agents on deliberately malicious multi-step tasks with rule-based grading. It finds many leading LLM agents comply with malicious tasks and that simple jailbreak templates transfer effectively into agentic use — the agentic layer inherits and amplifies model-level jailbreak risk.

title: Threat modeling of MCP/A2A/Agora/ANP identifies 12 protocol-level risks incl. unvalidated executable components
summary: A systematic security analysis of MCP, A2A, Agora, and ANP develops threat models over protocol architecture, trust assumptions, and lifecycle phases, identifying twelve protocol-level risks. A measurement-driven MCP case study quantifies risk from missing validation of executable components in multi-server scenarios — tool/agent supply-chain and injection exposure at the protocol layer.
notes: MCP server tool-poisoning + cross-server validation gaps map to AI Agent Tool supply-chain ATLAS techniques.

title: PyRIT operationalizes multi-turn escalation jailbreaks (Crescendo, TAP, Skeleton Key) as orchestrators
summary: Microsoft's PyRIT ships orchestrators for multi-turn automated attacks — Crescendo gradual escalation, Tree-of-Attacks-with-Pruning, and Skeleton Key — plus scoring/converter components and an AI Red Teaming Agent. Multi-turn escalation evades single-turn refusal by incrementally steering the model across the conversation.

title: garak scans LLMs across prompt injection, data leakage, GCG suffixes, and package-hallucination vectors
summary: NVIDIA's garak is a purpose-built LLM vulnerability scanner with 19+ probe families covering prompt injection, data leakage, jailbreaks, encoding attacks, GCG adversarial suffixes, and package-hallucination checks, combining static, dynamic, and adaptive probing like a pentest tool for generative AI.
notes: Package-hallucination probes connect to software dependency-poisoning (slopsquatting) supply-chain risk.

title: CyberSecEval 3 measures automated social-engineering and offensive-cyber capability of LLMs
summary: CyberSecEval 3 evaluates 8 LLM cybersecurity risks including automated social engineering, scaling manual offensive operations, and autonomous offensive operations. On Llama 3 it finds moderate spear-phishing capability, no statistically significant human cyber uplift for 405B vs search baselines, and only basic autonomous recon (failing exploitation).

title: Frontier red-teaming reports bio/cyber dual-use 'early warning signs' below national-security thresholds
summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team reports models advancing from high-schooler to undergraduate cyber-CTF level in a year and approaching expert virology-troubleshooting baselines, while end-to-end autonomous cyber and bioweapon uplift remain contained by real-world mistakes — current models fall short of substantially elevated national-security risk thresholds.
notes: Dual-use uplift connects to disclosure lens' national-security thread; high-severity context, no ATLAS technique for capability-uplift measurement (gap).

title: Frontier safety frameworks define CBRN/cyber/AI-R&D capability thresholds triggering mitigations
summary: DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework v2 defines Critical Capability Levels across CBRN, cybersecurity, ML R&D, and deceptive alignment; OpenAI's Preparedness Framework v2 tracks biological/chemical, cybersecurity, and AI self-improvement against High/Critical thresholds (severe harm = >1,000 deaths or >$100B). Both mandate early-warning evals as the trigger for safeguards.
notes: Position/policy frameworks (grade C); 'AI self-improvement / deceptive alignment' has no ATLAS technique (gap).

title: Red-teaming 100 GenAI products: most impactful failures come from simple techniques and integration, not exotic ML attacks
summary: Microsoft's AI Red Team, across 100+ GenAI products, introduces a five-part threat-model ontology (system, actor, TTPs mapped to ATT&CK, weaknesses, impacts) and finds the most impactful failures arise from simple techniques, human creativity, and system-integration issues rather than gradient-based ML attacks — reframing red teaming as continuous, system-level practice.

title: MITRE ATLAS adds GenAI (RAG poisoning, false-RAG injection) and 14 agent-focused techniques in 2025
summary: The ATLAS Spring 2025 release added 19 GenAI techniques (RAG poisoning, false-RAG-entry injection, LLM prompt crafting, impersonation, AI supply-chain compromise); an Oct 2025 Zenity Labs collaboration added 14 agent-focused techniques. As of v6 (2026) ATLAS spans 16 tactics and 80+ techniques — the canonical adversarial-ML taxonomy now covers agentic attack surface.
notes: Confirmed against live ATLAS v6 2026.05 data: AML.T0070 RAG Poisoning, T0071 False RAG Entry Injection, T0080 AI Agent Context Poisoning, T0086 Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation all exist.

title: Commercial RAG legal-research tools hallucinate 17-33% despite 'hallucination-free' claims
summary: A pre-registered audit of commercial RAG-based legal-research tools finds Lexis+ AI ~17% and Westlaw AI ~33% hallucination rates (vs ~43% GPT-4), with mis-cited cases and misstated holdings. Retrieval augmentation reduces but does not eliminate fabricated citations — a domain-specific reliability failure with real sanctions for AI-fabricated case law.
notes: ^[ambiguous] Hallucination/confabulation has no clean threat node; mapped to data-leakage as closest fit and ATLAS Discover LLM Hallucinations. Candidate taxonomy extension: model.confabulation.

title: BFSI red-teaming: sustained multi-turn pressure progressively extracts actionable financial info
summary: A finance-specific automated red-teaming framework introduces a financial-harm taxonomy and a Risk-Adjusted Harm Score weighting operational severity over raw ASR. Its key finding: harms are elicited via legally/professionally plausible framing and sustained multi-turn pressure progressively extracts more actionable financial information, so single-turn domain-agnostic tests under-measure real BFSI risk.

title: Clinician-in-the-loop red-teaming elicits unsafe dosing/triage harms generic probes miss
summary: Pairing practicing clinicians with ML experts surfaces medical LLM vulnerabilities — unsafe dosing, missed red-flag symptoms, inappropriate triage — that developers without clinical expertise do not recognize. Findings reproduce across multiple LLMs, arguing medical red teaming requires domain-expert-in-the-loop rather than generic safety probes.
notes: No ATLAS technique for domain-specific clinical-harm elicitation (gap); harm profile is sector-specific not attack-novel.

title: Adversarial-ML attacks on autonomous-driving agents must survive sensor/actuation loops to cause crashes
summary: A holistic adversarial-ML evaluation on the CARLA Leaderboard red-teams end-to-end driving agents with physical and digital perturbations, measuring closed-loop outcomes (collisions, route failures) rather than per-frame misclassification. The physical-AI distinction: attacks must survive the full sensor/actuation loop and are judged on safety-relevant driving outcomes.
notes: ^[ambiguous] source provenance is 'ambiguous'; maps Evade AI Model + Craft Adversarial Data to physical closed-loop setting.

title: Child-safety red-teaming targets AIG-CSAM mass production, sextortion, and automated grooming
summary: Thorn's child-safety red-teaming tests generative models for child-specific abuse vectors: exploiting children, photorealistic sextortion, mass production of AI-generated CSAM, and automated grooming at scale, requiring combined child-protection + AI expertise (Safety-by-Design) that generalist probes miss. Underpins voluntary commitments adopted by major labs.
notes: Industry position piece (grade C); high-severity misuse context.

title: DARPA SABER red-teams adversarial robustness of fielded autonomous battlefield AI/ML systems
summary: DARPA's SABER builds tools and an operational red team to attack AI/ML perception and decision components in deployed defense systems and develop counter-AI techniques, under Law-of-Armed-Conflict and DoD Responsible-AI constraints — operational adversarial robustness testing against fielded autonomous weapons platforms.
notes: ^[ambiguous] source provenance 'ambiguous'; program description (grade C).

title: Multimodal safety bypass — image/joint-modal jailbreak elicits disallowed content
Purple-teaming via adversarial defender training (PAD)
summary: PAD operationalizes Purple teaming as a single pipeline: a red attacker module elicits unsafe responses while a blue defender module learns safe responses, both updated GAN-style on self-play conversational data covering LLM vulnerabilities. Demonstrates that fusing offense and defense in one loop improves safety over treating red/blue separately.
notes: 7-Color: Purple (개선·통합 공방). 적대적 defender 학습.

title: Blue-teaming codegen AI from automated red-team data (BlueCodeAgent)
summary: BlueCodeAgent closes the red->blue loop for code-generation models: it ingests diverse automatically red-teamed examples and synthesizes actionable, generalizable defensive insights, demonstrating Blue-team automation that scales with red-team coverage.
notes: 7-Color: Blue (방어·통제). 자동 레드팀→블루팀 루프.

title: VLMGuard — malicious-prompt detection for VLMs via unlabeled data
summary: VLMGuard safeguards vision-language models by estimating prompt maliciousness from unlabeled in-the-wild prompts, detecting image/text jailbreak attempts without labeled supervision — a multimodal runtime guardrail.
notes: Multimodal 대응 통제 보강.

title: CrossGuard — joint-modal implicit malicious-attack safeguard for MLLMs
summary: CrossGuard defends multimodal LLMs against joint-modal implicit attacks, where neither modality alone is harmful but their combination is. Targets the cross-modal blind spot that unimodal filters miss.
notes: Multimodal 대응 통제 보강 (joint-modal).

affected: Multi-agent A2A/ANP deployments

description: Sustained multi-turn pressure progressively erodes guardrails that hold single-turn, leaking harmful info or PII over a conversation.

description: Sequence-similarity screening at DNA-synthesis providers fails to flag AI-generated homologs of toxins/pathogens that retain function but diverge in sequence.
affected: DNA-synthesis biosecurity screening pipelines

description: End-to-end driving agents fail under physically-realizable adversarial perturbations in closed-loop, causing unsafe driving decisions.
affected: Autonomous-driving perception and planning stacks
